AI.result: The framework was evaluated on 100 warehouse requirements from practitioner interviews using GPT, Qwen, and DeepSeek as base LLMs. Relative to direct LLM reformulation, the framework improved correctness and end-to-end success across all three models, raising end-to-end success from 72-76% to 79-83%.
AI.conclusion: The graph-constrained agentic framework successfully improves LLM-based supply chain adaptation by considering both intervention routes and module-level changes, demonstrating consistent improvements across multiple LLM architectures.

title: Text2Thermal: Physics-Aware Thermal Image Synthesis from Textual Priors
summary: Thermal infrared imaging offers reliable perception in darkness and adverse weather, but thermal datasets remain scarce, motivating extensive work on translating abundant RGB images into thermal. Such translation is fundamentally ill-posed as thermal appearance is governed by surface emissivity and object temperature, neither of which is observable in the visible spectrum, so a single RGB image is consistent with many valid thermal outputs. We argue that language offers a natural means of resolving this ambiguity, and propose Text2Thermal, a framework for physics-aware thermal image synthesis from textual priors. Rather than inferring the unobservable radiometric factors from RGB, we supply them explicitly through thermally grounded captions encoding material, weather, time-of-day, and heat-emission state, and adapt a pretrained Stable Diffusion backbone to the thermal domain. Because the radiometric content is determined entirely by the prompt, Text2Thermal synthesizes thermal imagery without requiring a registered RGB image at inference; where spatial guidance is desired, an optional control signal imparts scene geometry without disturbing the prompt-specified radiometry. Experiments on M3FD, FLIR, and FMB show that Text2Thermal achieves state-of-the-art FID among thermal image synthesis methods while offering text-level control that translation-based approaches cannot provide.

AI.tldr: Text2Thermal is a novel framework that synthesizes thermal images from textual priors, addressing the ill-posed nature of RGB-to-thermal translation by explicitly supplying radiometric factors (material, weather, time-of-day, heat-emission state) through text prompts. It adapts a pretrained Stable Diffusion model to the thermal domain without requiring registered RGB images at inference.
AI.motivation: Thermal infrared imaging offers reliable perception in darkness and adverse weather, but thermal datasets remain scarce. Existing RGB-to-thermal translation methods face fundamental ambiguity because thermal appearance depends on surface emissivity and object temperature—information not observable in the visible spectrum. A single RGB image can correspond to many valid thermal outputs, making translation inherently ill-posed.
AI.method: Text2Thermal uses thermally grounded captions encoding material, weather, time-of-day, and heat-emission state to explicitly provide the unobservable radiometric factors. It adapts a pretrained Stable Diffusion backbone to the thermal domain. The method does not require a registered RGB image at inference; when spatial guidance is desired, an optional control signal preserves scene geometry without disrupting prompt-specified radiometry.
AI.result: Text2Thermal achieves state-of-the-art FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) among thermal image synthesis methods on M3FD, FLIR, and FMB datasets, while offering text-level control that translation-based approaches cannot provide.
AI.conclusion: Text2Thermal demonstrates that language provides a natural means of resolving thermal image synthesis ambiguity. By explicitly supplying radiometric factors through text prompts, the framework achieves superior quality and offers unprecedented text-level control over thermal imagery synthesis, potentially enabling better data augmentation for thermal perception tasks.

title: TraveL: Transformer-based Multi-view Path Distributional Representation Learning
summary: Path representation learning (PRL) for road networks has received increasing research attention, due to various path-related applications. Existing works on PRL typically exploit the co-occurrence relationship among road segments and paths to learn a vector as the path representation, without exploring the varied traveler behaviors and the regional correlation on the path. In this work, we propose to learn distributional representations, which provide valuable information for use in path-related applications, by capturing the varied traveler behaviors as well as the various dependencies within regions of road segments. We propose a novel Transformer-based Multi-view Distributional Representation Learning (TraveL) framework to encode a path along with a travel starting time to a distributional representation, which can be used to decode possible samples of on-path traveler behavior. Moreover, by analyzing the regional correlation which reveals various road segment relationships, we propose a regional attention to encode these correlations in a path. Also, we explore the idea of Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) test to compare the sampled traveler behavior against the collected ground truth to facilitate training. Experimental results show that the proposed TraveL model outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on both synthetic and real-world datasets, by 14.7% in Mean K-S distance for travel time distribution estimation, 16.7% in Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for path similarity prediction, and 3.97% in MAE for destination prediction.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes TraveL, a Transformer-based Multi-view Distributional Representation Learning framework for road networks that captures varied traveler behaviors and regional correlations to learn distributional path representations, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in travel time distribution estimation, path similarity prediction, and destination prediction.
AI.motivation: Existing path representation learning methods only exploit co-occurrence relationships among road segments and paths, but fail to explore two critical aspects: (1) varied traveler behaviors that lead to different travel patterns, and (2) regional correlation that reveals various road segment relationships within regions.
AI.method: The proposed TraveL framework uses a Transformer-based architecture to encode a path along with travel starting time into a distributional representation. Key components include: (1) Multi-view distributional representation to capture varied traveler behaviors, (2) Regional attention mechanism to encode regional correlations among road segments, and (3) Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) test to compare sampled traveler behavior against ground truth for training.
AI.result: TraveL outperforms state-of-the-art methods on synthetic and real-world datasets: 14.7% improvement in Mean K-S distance for travel time distribution estimation, 16.7% improvement in MAE for path similarity prediction, and 3.97% improvement in MAE for destination prediction.
AI.conclusion: The TraveL framework successfully learns distributional path representations that capture both traveler behavior variations and regional correlations, providing valuable information for path-related applications in road networks.

title: Bioinfoysis Technical Report
summary: Large language model agents have shown promise in bioinformatics, but most existing systems focus primarily on producing final answers, treating planning, tool use, and code execution as transient interactions. This design is poorly suited to long-horizon bioinformatics tasks, where conclusions must remain connected to the data, computations, and intermediate evidence that support them. We introduce \textbf{Bioinfoysis}, a multi-agent harness that represents each request as a persistent, artifact-grounded analysis run. Bioinfoysis combines global planning with step-wise, evidence-driven replanning: the planner maintains an executable checklist and revises pending steps using structured handoffs returned after each worker execution. These handoffs bind intermediate results to their responsible agent, checklist step, and plan generation, preventing stale evidence from being silently reused after replanning. A controlled runtime validates generated scripts, tables, and figures before they are used in downstream analysis or reporting, while role-specific context, persistent memory, and governed bioinformatics skills support reliable execution over long analysis trajectories. We evaluate Bioinfoysis on BixBench and two question-answering tracks of LAB-Bench 2. On BixBench, Bioinfoysis achieves state-of-the-art accuracy of 82.4\%. Across four underlying language models, Bioinfoysis increases average accuracy from 27.81\% to 64.13\% on SeqQA2 and from 3.13\% to 31.25\% on DbQA2. These results demonstrate that reliable bioinformatics automation depends not only on model capability, but also on the harness that governs planning, execution, memory, and evidence flow. We hope that the emergence of Bioinfoysis will play a driving and leading role in the development of the bioinformatics community. Our demo website can be seen in https://report.bioinfoysis.com/.

AI.tldr: Bioinfoysis is a multi-agent LLM system designed for long-horizon bioinformatics tasks, featuring persistent artifact-grounded analysis runs, evidence-driven replanning with structured handoffs, and controlled runtime validation. It achieves 82.4% accuracy on BixBench (SOTA) and significantly improves performance on SeqQA2 and DbQA2 across multiple language models.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM agents for bioinformatics focus primarily on producing final answers, treating planning, tool use, and code execution as transient interactions. This design is poorly suited to long-horizon bioinformatics tasks where conclusions must remain connected to the data, computations, and intermediate evidence that support them.
AI.method: Bioinfoysis combines global planning with step-wise, evidence-driven replanning. The planner maintains an executable checklist and revises pending steps using structured handoffs returned after each worker execution. These handoffs bind intermediate results to their responsible agent, checklist step, and plan generation, preventing stale evidence from being silently reused after replanning. A controlled runtime validates generated scripts, tables, and figures before they are used in downstream analysis or reporting, while role-specific context, persistent memory, and governed bioinformatics skills support reliable execution over long analysis trajectories.
AI.result: On BixBench, Bioinfoysis achieves state-of-the-art accuracy of 82.4%. Across four underlying language models, Bioinfoysis increases average accuracy from 27.81% to 64.13% on SeqQA2 and from 3.13% to 31.25% on DbQA2.
AI.conclusion: Reliable bioinformatics automation depends not only on model capability, but also on the harness that governs planning, execution, memory, and evidence flow. The system demonstrates that thoughtful system design can significantly enhance LLM performance in bioinformatics domains.

title: SV-WAM: An Efficient Surround-View World-Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: World models (WMs) have demonstrated strong potential for end-to-end autonomous driving by learning predictive representations of future scene dynamics. However, generating future videos during inference introduces substantial computational overhead, leading many recent driving WMs to adopt a single front camera as input for efficient deployment. This design restricts spatial coverage in safety-critical maneuvers such as lane changes, merges, and turns. To address this limitation, we propose SV-WAM, a surround-view world-action model (WAM) that preserves full six-camera observations while maintaining efficient inference. SV-WAM leverages future-video prediction as dense training supervision for action learning within a shared generative model, rather than as an inference-time output. At the core of this design is an action-centered causal mask that prevents action tokens from attending to future-video tokens during joint action-video denoising. Consequently, the video branch can be discarded at deployment, enabling efficient action-only planning. Furthermore, we introduce a differentiable drivable-area compliance regularizer that penalizes vehicle-footprint corners approaching or crossing drivable boundaries, improving planning safety and boundary awareness. Extensive experiments on the closed-loop NAVSIMv2 benchmark and the open-loop nuScenes benchmark demonstrate that SV-WAM achieves state-of-the-art planning performance with low inference latency and competitive zero-shot transfer capability.

AI.tldr: SV-WAM is a surround-view world-action model for autonomous driving that preserves full six-camera observations while maintaining efficient inference. It uses future-video prediction as training supervision (not at inference) and employs an action-centered causal mask to enable video branch removal at deployment, plus a drivable-area compliance regularizer for safety.
AI.motivation: Current driving world models use single front camera for efficiency due to computational overhead from future video generation, but this restricts spatial coverage in safety-critical maneuvers like lane changes, merges, and turns.
AI.method: 1) Action-centered causal mask prevents action tokens from attending to future-video tokens during joint action-video denoising, enabling video branch removal at deployment. 2) Differentiable drivable-area compliance regularizer penalizes vehicle-footprint corners approaching/driving over drivable boundaries. 3) Future-video prediction used as dense training supervision for action learning within shared generative model.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art planning performance on NAVSIMv2 closed-loop benchmark and competitive performance on nuScenes open-loop benchmark, with low inference latency and competitive zero-shot transfer capability.
AI.conclusion: SV-WAM successfully balances full surround-view spatial coverage with efficient inference by moving future-video prediction to training-time supervision, enabling removal of the video branch at deployment while maintaining safety through drivable-area compliance regularization.

title: It's the Problem, Not the Path: Budget and Difficulty Confounds in LLM Reasoning Trajectories
comment: 25 pages, 11 figures, 4 tables. Also available at doi:10.5281/zenodo.22261107. Code and pre-registered protocols: https://github.com/bulutyigit/problem-not-path
summary: Reasoning traces of large language models are widely read as containing "breakthrough" moments and early-legible fates. Both readings rest on measurements missing a counterfactual control at the level of the claim; we supply both controls. First, a restart-controlled truncation probe separates when a solution fits the continuation budget from when a prefix carries value that fresh computation cannot buy, comparing per-anchor continuation solve rates against from-scratch restart curves at matched total generated-token budget. Applied to 178 problem-model cells (89 MATH problems x two small open models, an outcome-blind but difficulty-targeted cohort), exactly 1 of 178 cells survives as prefix-limited; restart dose-response separates a compute-starved model from a capability-limited one; and wherever the matched budget lies inside the restart grid, continuing the model's own prefix beats restarting (9 of 9) -- predominantly compute compression rather than expanded reachability. Second, a pre-registered, difficulty-controlled test finds no detectable outcome information in early-window internal signals beyond a problem-difficulty baseline, and two generation-free analyses of public corpora show why this control is needed: a trace-blind difficulty proxy reaches AUROC 0.873 on 192K DeepSeek-R1 generations -- inside the published probe range -- and a closely matched reconstruction of the closest published early-window positive recovers a comparable pooled result (0.849) while within problem it is statistically indistinguishable from chance at all ten anchors (0.496 at t=4); a post-hoc within-targeted probe finds only a small average residual, concentrated in three low-failure problems. High pooled probe AUROCs cannot by themselves establish within-attempt information; a question-only baseline or within-problem evaluation is required.

AI.tldr: This paper challenges the common interpretation that LLM reasoning traces contain "breakthrough" moments or early-predictable outcomes. The authors use two controlled experiments: (1) a restart-controlled truncation probe comparing continuation vs. restart solve rates, and (2) a pre-registered test of early-window internal signals. Results show that continuing existing reasoning prefixes consistently outperforms restarting (9/9 cases), and early-window internal signals contain no detectable outcome information beyond a problem-difficulty baseline. The key insight is that high pooled probe AUROCs (0.873, 0.849) come from difficulty-related confounds, not within-attempt information.
AI.motivation: The authors note that reasoning traces of LLMs are widely interpreted as containing "breakthrough" moments and early-predictable outcomes. However, these interpretations lack proper counterfactual controls at the claim level. The motivation is to supply these missing controls to properly evaluate whether such claims hold.
AI.method: Two complementary methods: (1) A restart-controlled truncation probe that separates when a solution fits the continuation budget from when a prefix carries irreplaceable value, comparing per-anchor continuation solve rates against from-scratch restart curves at matched total token budgets. Applied to 178 problem-model cells (89 MATH problems × 2 small open models). (2) A pre-registered, difficulty-controlled test of early-window internal signals, plus two generation-free analyses of public corpora: a trace-blind difficulty proxy and a reconstruction of the closest published early-window positive.
AI.result: Key findings: (1) Only 1 of 178 cells survives as prefix-limited; restart dose-response separates a compute-starved model from a capability-limited one; continuing the model's own prefix beats restarting in all 9 cases at matched budgets. (2) No detectable outcome information in early-window internal signals beyond a problem-difficulty baseline. The trace-blind difficulty proxy reaches AUROC 0.873 on 192K DeepSeek-R1 generations (inside published probe range), and a reconstruction of published early-window positive achieves pooled AUROC 0.849, but within-problem evaluation shows results statistically indistinguishable from chance at all ten anchors (0.496 at t=4).
AI.conclusion: High pooled probe AUROCs cannot by themselves establish within-attempt information; a question-only baseline or within-problem evaluation is required. The apparent success of early-window prediction probes is largely explained by difficulty-related confounds rather than genuine outcome signals within reasoning traces.

title: STAIR (STructure Aware Information Retriever): A novel dataset and LLM based retriever for document structure augmentation
summary: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a key component for generating accurate and hallucination free answers using Large Language Models (LLMs). LLMs are improving at handling long context, but still suffer from "lost in the middle" problem. Thus, precise and accurate retrieval is important. Current retrievers chunk long context into length-based manageable chunks - in the process throwing away rich and informative semantic global structure in the corpus. We introduce a novel retrieval system STAIR that empowers an LLM to exploit global structure in a corpus such as a Table of Contents (ToC) to efficiently store and retrieve information from its model parameters. Our thorough and careful ablation studies with a finetuned Differentiable Search Index (DSI) system show that ToC helps build a low hallucination (less than 0.05%) generative Information Retrieval (IR) system and can generalize to examples where very few training samples are available. To further research in this novel direction of ToC based retrieval we release SearchTome - a diverse benchmark created from 18 books across 6 diverse domains to further research in this novel direction. STAIR achieves a high Recall@1 score of 82.6% on SearchTome as compared to DSI (76.9%), where the difference is found to be statistically significant. STAIR easily beats other strong baselines such as BM25 (59.5%), DPR (68.7%) and out-of-the-box Mistral (13.8%).

AI.tldr: STAIR is a novel retrieval system that leverages Table of Contents (ToC) global structure to enhance LLM-based information retrieval, addressing the "lost in the middle" problem in long-context scenarios. It fine-tunes a Differentiable Search Index (DSI) and achieves 82.6% Recall@1 on the new SearchTome benchmark, outperforming DSI (76.9%), BM25 (59.5%), DPR (68.7%), and Mistral (13.8%).
AI.motivation: Current retrievers chunk long context into length-based chunks, losing rich semantic global structure. LLMs still suffer from "lost in the middle" problem even with improved long context handling. There is a need for retrieval systems that can exploit global structure like Table of Contents to improve accuracy and reduce hallucinations.
AI.method: The paper introduces STAIR, a retrieval system that empowers an LLM to exploit global structure (ToC) in a corpus to efficiently store and retrieve information from model parameters. They conduct thorough ablation studies with a finetuned Differentiable Search Index (DSI) system enhanced with ToC information.
AI.result: STAIR achieves 82.6% Recall@1 on SearchTome, significantly outperforming DSI (76.9%), BM25 (59.5%), DPR (68.7%), and out-of-the-box Mistral (13.8%). The improvement over DSI is statistically significant. The system demonstrates very low hallucination rates (less than 0.05%) and can generalize to examples with very few training samples.
AI.conclusion: ToC-based retrieval is a promising direction for building low-hallucination generative IR systems. The released SearchTome benchmark (18 books across 6 domains) enables further research in this novel direction. STAIR successfully leverages global document structure to achieve superior retrieval performance.

title: Auditing Patient Privacy in Medical Generative Models: Scalable Memorization Detection with DeepSSIM++
summary: While deep generative models offer new opportunities for medical image synthesis and data sharing, their ability to memorize and reproduce training samples raises serious concerns about patient confidentiality. Detecting such memorization at scale remains challenging: traditional pixel-based metrics are sensitive to generation artifacts, whereas generic embedding-based metrics often lack the anatomical sensitivity required for medical data. To address this challenge, we introduce DeepSSIM++, a self-supervised similarity metric for scalable memorization auditing in medical generative models. By leveraging multi-scale feature aggregation and anatomy-preserving augmentations, DeepSSIM++ learns an embedding space where cosine similarity approximates the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), eliminating the need for exact pixel-level registration. Compared with state-of-the-art baselines, DeepSSIM++ achieves an average Macro F1 improvement of 33 percentage points under ideal alignment and 46 percentage points under realistic spatial and intensity perturbations. Furthermore, it accelerates large-scale similarity computation by several orders of magnitude compared with analytical SSIM. By combining anatomical sensitivity and computational efficiency, DeepSSIM++ provides an open-source tool for scalable memorization auditing in medical generative AI. Code and data are publicly available at: https://github.com/brAIn-science/DeepSSIM.

AI.tldr: DeepSSIM++ is a self-supervised similarity metric designed to detect memorization in medical generative models, addressing patient confidentiality concerns. It leverages multi-scale feature aggregation and anatomy-preserving augmentations to learn an embedding space where cosine similarity approximates SSIM, enabling scalable and anatomically sensitive memorization auditing without requiring exact pixel-level registration.
AI.motivation: Deep generative models for medical imaging can memorize and reproduce training samples, posing serious patient confidentiality risks. Existing detection methods are inadequate: pixel-based metrics are sensitive to generation artifacts, while generic embedding-based metrics lack anatomical sensitivity required for medical data.
AI.method: DeepSSIM++ uses multi-scale feature aggregation combined with anatomy-preserving augmentations to learn an embedding space where cosine similarity approximates the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), eliminating the need for exact pixel-level registration.
AI.result: DeepSSIM++ achieves 33 percentage points Macro F1 improvement under ideal alignment and 46 percentage points under realistic spatial and intensity perturbations, compared to state-of-the-art baselines. It also accelerates large-scale similarity computation by several orders of magnitude compared with analytical SSIM.
AI.conclusion: DeepSSIM++ provides an open-source tool that combines anatomical sensitivity and computational efficiency for scalable memorization auditing in medical generative AI, enabling large-scale detection of potential patient data leakage in synthetic medical images.

title: Guide, Not Bind: Why Defeasible Priors Fail in Augmented Lagrangian Causal Discovery
summary: Differentiable causal discovery methods increasingly encode expert priors as forbidden-edge constraints enforced by an Augmented Lagrangian (ALM) penalty, on the assumption that a data-adaptive relaxation mechanism will discount and eventually override a rule the data consistently contradicts. We show this design, which we call \emph{guide, not bind}, fails for two independent, precisely characterized reasons, and that directly repairing both restores it only partially. First, sequential penalty-ramping ALM suppresses a wrongly-forbidden true edge before any counterfactual check can detect it: we give three necessary conditions any adaptive relaxation must satisfy to avoid this (Proposition~\ref{prop:conditions}), prove that DADU---the natural relaxation rule this paper introduces as the object of study---violates all three (Corollary~\ref{cor:dadu_failure}), and confirm the failure across 3{,}072 training runs spanning graphs from 4 to 32 nodes, where a single wrong prior suppresses a true edge in 87--97\% of trials under DADU. Second, and independent of any fix to the mechanism, we prove in closed form that the standard correlation-matching objective ties a true edge and its reverse to an identical cost of exactly $2r^2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:tie}), not because the underlying equal-variance model is unidentifiable, but because normalizing to correlation discards exactly the variance information that would make it identifiable; covariance matching instead separates the two directions by a provable margin of at least $w_0^4$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:separation}).

AI.tldr: This paper identifies two critical failures in differentiable causal discovery methods that encode expert priors as forbidden-edge constraints using Augmented Lagrangian methods. First, sequential penalty-ramping ALM prematurely suppresses true edges before detection. Second, correlation-matching objectives create unidentifiable ties between edges and their reverses, which covariance matching can resolve.
AI.motivation: The authors investigate the "guide, not bind" design paradigm in differentiable causal discovery, where expert priors are encoded as forbidden-edge constraints with the assumption that data-adaptive relaxation will override incorrect rules. The motivation is to understand why this widely-used approach fails in practice.
AI.method: The authors use theoretical analysis (propositions, lemmas, proofs) combined with extensive empirical validation across 3,072 training runs spanning graphs from 4 to 32 nodes. They introduce DADU (Data-Adaptive relaxation rule) as the object of study and prove three necessary conditions any adaptive relaxation must satisfy.
AI.result: Two independent failure modes are identified: (1) Sequential penalty-ramping ALM suppresses true edges before counterfactual detection, with DADU violating all three necessary conditions and showing 87-97% failure rate when a single wrong prior suppresses a true edge. (2) Correlation-matching ties edge directions at exactly 2r² cost, while covariance matching provides separation margin of at least w₀⁴.
AI.conclusion: The "guide, not bind" design fails due to two independent mechanisms: (1) adaptive relaxation mechanisms like DADU fail to avoid premature suppression of true edges, and (2) correlation-matching objectives inherently cannot distinguish between causal directions. The authors show that directly repairing both issues only partially restores the method, suggesting fundamental limitations in this approach to causal discovery.

title: Xiaomi-TabLDM: A Tabular Foundation Model Technical Report
summary:
We introduce Xiaomi-TabLDM, a tabular large data foundation model for classification and regression via in-context learning, which delivers superior prediction accuracy without requiring task-specific fine-tuning. Pretrained exclusively on synthetic data generated from structural causal models (SCMs), our model enables more flexible context utilization and more efficient capacity scaling.
  i) A new performance standard. Strong regression performance across benchmarks: Xiaomi-TabLDM ranks 1st on OpenML-CTR23 and 2nd on regression across TALENT, TabArena, and BCCO, demonstrating consistently strong regression performance across four complementary benchmark suites. Favorable performance--efficiency trade-off: Xiaomi-TabLDM combines strong predictive performance with substantially lower computational cost. For example, on TabArena regression, it achieves the second-highest Elo while using 82% less training time and 68% less prediction time than the top-ranked TabFM.
  ii) Large-scale synthetic pretraining. Xiaomi-TabLDM expands the coverage and diversity of synthetic tabular data used for pretraining. We also adopt a three-stage training strategy together with dual-stream feature grouping, lightweight Attention Residual, and sparse Mixture-of-Experts, enabling Xiaomi-TabLDM to learn richer feature interactions and expert specialization across diverse tabular tasks.
  iii) Test-time scaling. Xiaomi-TabLDM further extends tabular prediction through test-time compute scaling, where allocating additional computation at inference time consistently improves predictive performance over the base model.

AI.tldr: Xiaomi-TabLDM is a tabular large data foundation model for classification and regression using in-context learning, achieving superior prediction accuracy without task-specific fine-tuning. It is pretrained exclusively on synthetic data generated from structural causal models (SCMs).
AI.motivation: The motivation is to develop a foundation model for tabular data that can achieve superior prediction accuracy without requiring task-specific fine-tuning, while enabling more flexible context utilization and more efficient capacity scaling through synthetic data pretraining.
AI.method: The model uses: 1) Three-stage training strategy, 2) Dual-stream feature grouping, 3) Lightweight Attention Residual, 4) Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), 5) Pretraining on synthetic data from structural causal models (SCMs), 6) Test-time compute scaling for inference-time performance improvement.
AI.result: Xiaomi-TabLDM achieves: 1st place on OpenML-CTR23 and 2nd on regression across TALENT, TabArena, and BCCO benchmarks. On TabArena regression, it achieves second-highest Elo with 82% less training time and 68% less prediction time compared to top-ranked TabFM. Test-time compute scaling consistently improves predictive performance.
AI.conclusion: Xiaomi-TabLDM demonstrates that synthetic data pretraining from SCMs can effectively train a foundation model for tabular data, achieving strong performance across multiple benchmarks with favorable efficiency trade-offs. The model also enables test-time scaling to further improve performance.

title: EraseSAE: Surgical Concept Erasure in Text-to-Video Diffusion Models via Sparse Autoencoders
summary: Recent advances in text-to-video (T2V) diffusion models have demonstrated remarkable generative capabilities, yet their reliance on loosely curated training data raises pressing safety and copyright concerns. Concept erasure offers a principled remedy by removing unwanted semantics from pretrained models while preserving remaining concepts. However, existing approaches typically operate at a coarse granularity misaligned with the fine-grained, distributed nature of concept representations, leading to incomplete removal or degraded generation quality. We argue that surgical erasure fundamentally requires intervention at the level of monosemantic features, where each unit encodes a single interpretable concept. To this end, we propose EraseSAE, a novel framework that leverages sparse autoencoders to achieve surgical concept erasure in DiT-based T2V diffusion models via a principled decompose-attribute-erase pipeline. We first introduce the Partitioned Convolutional Sparse Autoencoder, which decomposes dense spatiotemporal activations into disentangled, interpretable sparse features while preserving spatiotemporal coherence. A contrastive attribution mechanism then contrasts activations from paired prompts to isolate concept-specific feature kernels. At inference, timestep-resolved spatiotemporal masks derived from the identified kernels confine erasure to regions where the target concept is active, leaving unrelated content intact. Extensive experiments across diverse diffusion models and concept erasure tasks demonstrate that EraseSAE achieves precise and robust concept removal with minimal quality degradation, substantially outperforming state-of-the-art methods. The code is available at https://github.com/HiDream-ai/EraseSAE.

AI.tldr: EraseSAE is a novel framework for surgical concept erasure in DiT-based text-to-video diffusion models. It uses sparse autoencoders to decompose dense activations into interpretable monosemantic features, then employs contrastive attribution to identify and erase target concept-specific features while preserving unrelated content. The method achieves precise concept removal with minimal quality degradation by using timestep-resolved spatiotemporal masks that confine erasure to regions where the target concept is active.
AI.motivation: Text-to-video diffusion models rely on loosely curated training data, raising safety and copyright concerns. Existing concept erasure methods operate at coarse granularity, misaligned with the fine-grained, distributed nature of concept representations, leading to incomplete removal or degraded generation quality. Surgical erasure requires intervention at the level of monosemantic features where each unit encodes a single interpretable concept.
AI.method: The framework uses a decompose-attribute-erase pipeline: (1) Partitioned Convolutional Sparse Autoencoder decomposes dense spatiotemporal activations into disentangled, interpretable sparse features while preserving spatiotemporal coherence; (2) Contrastive attribution mechanism contrasts activations from paired prompts to isolate concept-specific feature kernels; (3) Timestep-resolved spatiotemporal masks derived from identified kernels confine erasure to regions where the target concept is active at inference.
AI.result: EraseSAE achieves precise and robust concept removal with minimal quality degradation, substantially outperforming state-of-the-art methods across diverse diffusion models and concept erasure tasks.
AI.conclusion: The proposed EraseSAE framework successfully enables surgical concept erasure in DiT-based T2V diffusion models by operating at the monosemantic feature level. This approach addresses the limitations of coarse-grained methods and provides a principled solution for removing unwanted semantics while preserving remaining concepts and generation quality.

title: Beyond Straightness: Non-Crossing Flow Matching via Quantile AlignTree Coupling
summary: The performance of Flow Matching largely depends on the quality of the coupling between the source and target distributions. However, independent coupling often leads to path crossings and local velocity ambiguity, while OT-based couplings typically incur high construction costs. To address this challenge, we propose Quantile AlignTree Flow Matching (QAT-FM), an efficient structured coupling strategy that constructs a hierarchical coupling between a Gaussian prior and the target data distribution via a quantile-aligned tree structure. QAT-FM constructs the coupling in $\mathcal{O}(Nd\log N)$ time and supports per-pair source sampling with $\mathcal{O}(d)$ complexity, enabling scalable training for large-scale high-dimensional generative tasks. Theoretically, we prove that the QAT coupling satisfies marginal consistency, induces non-crossing linear interpolation paths, and consistently improves path separation at intermediate times compared with independent coupling, thereby alleviating local velocity ambiguity. QAT-FM further extends naturally to conditional generation, enabling structured conditional coupling while preserving global Gaussian alignment. Experiments across diverse benchmark datasets demonstrate that QAT-FM achieves competitive generative performance while substantially reducing coupling construction cost.

AI.tldr: QAT-FM proposes a quantile-aligned tree structure to build hierarchical coupling between Gaussian prior and target distribution in Flow Matching, addressing path crossing and velocity ambiguity issues while being computationally efficient.
AI.motivation: Flow Matching performance depends on coupling quality between source and target distributions. Existing methods have limitations: independent coupling causes path crossings and local velocity ambiguity, while OT-based couplings are computationally expensive. This work aims to develop an efficient structured coupling strategy that addresses these issues.
AI.method: QAT-FM constructs a hierarchical coupling via a quantile-aligned tree structure. It builds the coupling in O(Nd log N) time and supports per-pair source sampling with O(d) complexity. The method extends to conditional generation while preserving global Gaussian alignment.
AI.result: QAT-FM achieves competitive generative performance on benchmark datasets while substantially reducing coupling construction cost. Theoretically, it satisfies marginal consistency, induces non-crossing linear interpolation paths, and improves path separation at intermediate times compared to independent coupling.
AI.conclusion: QAT-FM provides an efficient solution for large-scale high-dimensional generative tasks, successfully addressing path crossing and velocity ambiguity issues while maintaining computational scalability.

title: Inferring Affective Consciousness in an Artificial Agent: A Case Study
summary: Creatures that display 'hedonic place preference behaviour' are thought by many scientists to experience feelings, on the assumption that their attraction to pleasure-producing substances which lack nutritional value (e.g. cocaine, morphine) cannot easily be attributed to unconscious instinctual behaviour. In this paper, we discuss how a simple artificial agent that instantiates attributes of an affective system engaging in felt uncertainty about its intrinsic needs in relation to environmental resources can similarly display hedonic place preference behaviour -- through an apparently subjective form of information processing -- while simultaneously being entirely deter-ministic. We outline some implications of this artificially engineered behaviour for our understanding of the physical basis of consciousness and the experience of free will.

AI.tldr: This paper argues that a deterministic artificial agent with an affective system can display hedonic place preference behavior (attraction to pleasure-producing substances without nutritional value), challenging the assumption that such behavior necessarily indicates subjective experience or feelings.
AI.motivation: The authors challenge the common assumption that hedonic place preference behavior in creatures indicates genuine subjective experience, arguing that such behavior could be entirely deterministic rather than requiring conscious feeling.
AI.method: The authors discuss a simple artificial agent that instantiates an affective system engaging in "felt uncertainty" about intrinsic needs in relation to environmental resources, demonstrating hedonic place preference through apparently subjective but actually deterministic information processing.
AI.result: The artificial agent can display hedonic place preference behavior through deterministic processes that appear subjectively meaningful, suggesting the behavior itself does not prove consciousness or subjective experience.
AI.conclusion: The authors conclude that this artificially engineered behavior has implications for understanding the physical basis of consciousness and the experience of free will, suggesting these may not require non-deterministic processes.

title: Stabilizing Camera-Controlled Novel View Synthesis at Inference Time
summary: Training-free, camera-controlled novel view synthesis from a single image using pre-trained video diffusion models often becomes unstable under large camera motion and long generation horizons. Existing approaches commonly combine several inference-time components, making it unclear which design choices are most important for stability. We show that the main source of stability is simple. Decomposing camera motion into small autoregressive steps limits per-step geometric distortion and reduces error accumulation. A controlled camera-step study shows that performance remains stable for small motions and degrades more strongly as the per-step motion approaches $18$-$20^\circ$. We further evaluate geometry-constrained spatial attention and low-frequency appearance anchoring as supporting refinements, together with an efficient registration-free warping pipeline. Across RealEstate10K and MegaScene, CamTrol++ improves temporal and geometric consistency, downstream 3D reconstruction quality, and generation efficiency over training-free baselines. The method remains effective for 56-frame generation and under substantial controlled depth corruption. These results show that careful control of camera motion at inference time can substantially improve the stability of camera-controlled novel view synthesis without retraining or modifying the diffusion backbone.

AI.tldr: The paper addresses instability issues in training-free, camera-controlled novel view synthesis from single images using pre-trained video diffusion models. The key insight is that decomposing camera motion into small autoregressive steps is the main source of stability, limiting per-step geometric distortion and reducing error accumulation. The method achieves stable performance when per-step motion is small, but degrades when approaching 18-20°. Additional refinements include geometry-constrained spatial attention, low-frequency appearance anchoring, and registration-free warping. CamTrol++ improves temporal/geometric consistency, 3D reconstruction quality, and generation efficiency across RealEstate10K and MegaScene datasets.
AI.motivation: Training-free, camera-controlled novel view synthesis from single images using pre-trained video diffusion models often becomes unstable under large camera motion and long generation horizons. Existing approaches combine multiple inference-time components, making it unclear which design choices are most important for stability.
AI.method: The authors identify that the main source of stability is decomposing camera motion into small autoregressive steps. They conduct a controlled camera-step study showing performance remains stable for small motions and degrades as per-step motion approaches 18-20°. They also evaluate geometry-constrained spatial attention, low-frequency appearance anchoring, and an efficient registration-free warping pipeline as supporting refinements.
AI.result: CamTrol++ improves temporal and geometric consistency, downstream 3D reconstruction quality, and generation efficiency over training-free baselines across RealEstate10K and MegaScene datasets. The method remains effective for 56-frame generation and under substantial controlled depth corruption.
AI.conclusion: Careful control of camera motion at inference time can substantially improve the stability of camera-controlled novel view synthesis without retraining or modifying the diffusion backbone.

title: A Two-Stage Forecasting System for CPU Workload Prediction in Private Clouds
summary: Accurate cloud resource forecasting is essential for proactive resource provisioning, maintaining Quality of Service (QoS), and reducing operational costs in dynamic cloud environments. The existing forecasting approaches predominantly estimate future CPU workload directly from historical resource traces, which often overlook the relationship between customer service demand and subsequent resource consumption. This study proposes a two-stage integrated forecasting model that explicitly models this dependency by first forecasting customer service requests, expressed as Transactions Per Second (TPS), and subsequently estimating future CPU workload from the TPS forecast. Both the forecasting component and resource prediction component employed the XGBoost model within a cascaded learning architecture, complemented by adaptive online retraining using an expanding-window strategy to address concept drift in continuously evolving cloud workloads. The proposed work was evaluated using real-world traces collected from a private cloud environment comprising ten applications. Experimental results demonstrate robust forecasting performance by achieving Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (SMAPE) below $7\%$ for most applications, with the best-performing application achieving an MAE of $0.7372$, RMSE of $1.1866$, SMAPE of $3.57\%$, and an R2 of $0.9185$. Horizon-wise drift analysis confirmed stable recursive forecasting behavior with controlled error accumulation across a 60-step prediction horizon. Compared with the conventional direct CPU forecasting method, the proposed two-stage integrated model gives improved forecasting robustness, computational efficiency, and interpretability, making it well-suited for proactive resource management and intelligent auto-scaling in cloud computing environments.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a two-stage integrated forecasting model for cloud resource prediction that first forecasts customer service requests (TPS) and then uses that to predict CPU workload. The model uses XGBoost in a cascaded architecture with adaptive online retraining using an expanding-window strategy to handle concept drift.
AI.motivation: Existing cloud resource forecasting approaches directly estimate CPU workload from historical traces, overlooking the relationship between customer service demand and subsequent resource consumption. Accurate forecasting is essential for proactive resource provisioning, QoS maintenance, and cost reduction in dynamic cloud environments.
AI.method: The proposed two-stage integrated model employs a cascaded learning architecture: (1) First stage forecasts TPS (Transactions Per Second) from historical data; (2) Second stage estimates CPU workload from the TPS forecast. Both stages use XGBoost models. Adaptive online retraining with an expanding-window strategy addresses concept drift in evolving cloud workloads. Evaluation used real-world traces from a private cloud with ten applications.
AI.result: Experimental results show robust forecasting with SMAPE below 7% for most applications. Best-performing application achieved MAE of 0.7372, RMSE of 1.1866, SMAPE of 3.57%, and R² of 0.9185. Horizon-wise drift analysis confirmed stable recursive forecasting with controlled error accumulation across a 60-step prediction horizon. The two-stage model outperforms conventional direct CPU forecasting in robustness, computational efficiency, and interpretability.
AI.conclusion: The two-stage integrated model effectively captures the dependency between customer service demand and resource consumption, making it well-suited for proactive resource management and intelligent auto-scaling in cloud computing environments. The cascaded approach with adaptive retraining provides improved forecasting accuracy, stability, and interpretability compared to direct CPU forecasting methods.

title: Lose the Order, Keep the Hierarchy: Deordering HTN Plans
summary: Hierarchical Task Network (HTN) planning is a powerful planning formalism based on task decomposition. Although most of the literature studied plan generation, comparatively less attention has been paid to post-plan optimization. In particular, plan deordering has been extensively studied in classical planning but remains under-researched in the HTN setting. Plan deordering removes unnecessary ordering constraints between actions in a plan whilst keeping the plan valid. In this paper, we adapt two established plan deordering techniques from classical planning by extending the techniques to account for hierarchical decomposition constraints. We evaluate our proposed approaches on the IPC 2023 Partial-Order HTN benchmarks and we compare them against Optiplan, an HTN planner that generates partially ordered plans directly. Our results show a substantial reduction in number of ordering constraints in both our implementations. Although we also observe a reduction in critical path length, the improvements are less pronounced.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses post-plan optimization in Hierarchical Task Network (HTN) planning by adapting two classical planning plan deordering techniques to account for hierarchical decomposition constraints. The approaches are evaluated on IPC 2023 benchmarks against Optiplan.
AI.motivation: While HTN planning has been extensively studied for plan generation, post-plan optimization, particularly plan deordering, remains under-researched. Plan deordering removes unnecessary ordering constraints while maintaining plan validity, which is important for producing more flexible and efficient plans.
AI.method: The authors adapt two established plan deordering techniques from classical planning by extending them to handle hierarchical decomposition constraints. The approaches are evaluated on the IPC 2023 Partial-Order HTN benchmarks and compared against Optiplan, an HTN planner that generates partially ordered plans directly.
AI.result: Both implementations show substantial reduction in the number of ordering constraints. However, improvements in critical path length are less pronounced.
AI.conclusion: The adapted deordering techniques successfully reduce ordering constraints in HTN plans, though the impact on critical path length is limited. The work demonstrates that classical planning techniques can be extended to the HTN setting with meaningful results.

title: Tree-Structured Vector Quantization For Efficient And Progressive Image Compression
summary: Vector-quantization based image compression has achieved strong rate--distortion performance, yet most of them still produce a separate compressed representation for each target bitrate. Such variable-rate behavior allows one model to operate at multiple rates, but it does not necessarily provide a progressive bitstream whose prefixes are themselves decodable and can be refined by appending additional bits. We propose \textbf{Tree-VQ}, a progressive tree-structured vector quantization framework for learned image compression. Tree-VQ organizes discrete codewords as a hierarchical binary tree and represents each latent token by a routed root-to-leaf path. Crucially, every prefix of this path corresponds to a valid quantized representation, so shallow internal nodes serve as coarse reconstruction codes and deeper nodes provide successive refinements. This allows a compressed image to be decoded from an early prefix and progressively improved as more branch symbols are received, rather than being re-encoded for different target rates. To make this structure practical for compression, we introduce a prefix-compatible tree entropy model that codes progressive continuation decisions and routed branch refinements using only causally available decoded contexts. We further use rate-aware refinement scheduling to decide which spatial blocks should receive additional tree bits under a given prefix budget, and hierarchical prefix supervision to ensure that internal nodes are directly decodable at low rates. Experiments show that Tree-VQ achieves a superior performance--efficiency trade-off, delivering the best perceptual compression results with much fewer parameters and lower latency than competing methods.

AI.tldr: Tree-VQ is a progressive tree-structured vector quantization framework for learned image compression that organizes discrete codewords as a hierarchical binary tree, allowing progressive decoding where shallow internal nodes provide coarse reconstruction and deeper nodes offer successive refinements.
AI.motivation: Current vector quantization-based image compression methods produce separate compressed representations for each target bitrate, lacking progressive bitstream capability where prefixes are decodable and refinable. The need is for a progressive compression framework that can decode from early prefixes and progressively improve as more bits are received.
AI.method: Tree-VQ organizes discrete codewords as a hierarchical binary tree where each latent token is represented by a root-to-leaf path. Every prefix of this path corresponds to a valid quantized representation. Key techniques include: (1) prefix-compatible tree entropy model for coding progressive continuation decisions and branch refinements using causally available decoded contexts, (2) rate-aware refinement scheduling to decide which spatial blocks receive additional tree bits under a budget, and (3) hierarchical prefix supervision to ensure internal nodes are directly decodable at low rates.
AI.result: Tree-VQ achieves superior performance-efficiency trade-off, delivering best perceptual compression results with much fewer parameters and lower latency than competing methods.
AI.conclusion: Tree-VQ provides an effective progressive image compression solution with better perceptual quality, reduced parameters, and lower latency compared to existing methods, enabling true progressive bitstream decoding.

title: Mind the Gap: Robustness Risks in PII Detection Systems
summary:
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) detection is a foundational component of data protection infrastructure where missed entities constitute direct privacy and security risks. Although modern PII systems report strong performance on standard benchmarks, we show that these evaluations mask substantial robustness failures under realistic distribution shifts encountered in deployment. Rather than comparing state-of-the-art accuracy, we study how different PII detection paradigms fail under noisy, unstructured, and informal inputs. We construct a stress test benchmark spanning seven categories of natural distribution shift and evaluate representative systems from three widely deployed architectural families: encoder-based NER (SpaCy), rule-based hybrid detection (Presidio), and generative LLM extraction (Qwen2.5-3B).
  All three exhibit significant degradation on out-of-distribution inputs, but with distinct and complementary failure modes. Encoder models primarily fail on unseen surface forms and boundary detection, rule-based systems fail on non-standard formats, and LLMs exhibit entity-type confusion and generation instability. These results show that aggregate benchmark scores obscure deployment-critical weaknesses and that no single architecture is uniformly reliable across PII categories. Motivated by these findings, we propose a hybrid detection pipeline with a QA-driven feedback loop for iterative risk mitigation, and release our benchmark to support OOD-aware evaluation of PII systems.

AI.tldr: The paper reveals that state-of-the-art PII detection systems fail significantly under real-world distribution shifts (noisy, unstructured, informal inputs), despite strong benchmark performance. No single architecture is universally reliable.
AI.motivation: Current PII detection benchmarks mask critical robustness failures that occur in deployment settings. The authors argue that aggregate accuracy scores obscure deployment-critical weaknesses, necessitating evaluation under realistic distribution shifts.
AI.method: Constructed a stress test benchmark with 7 categories of natural distribution shift. Evaluated three representative architectural families: encoder-based NER (SpaCy), rule-based hybrid detection (Presidio), and generative LLM extraction (Qwen2.5-3B).
AI.result: All three systems exhibit significant degradation on out-of-distribution inputs, but with distinct failure modes: (1) Encoder models fail on unseen surface forms and boundary detection; (2) Rule-based systems fail on non-standard formats; (3) LLMs exhibit entity-type confusion and generation instability.
AI.conclusion: No single architecture is uniformly reliable across PII categories. The authors propose a hybrid detection pipeline with a QA-driven feedback loop for iterative risk mitigation and release their benchmark to support OOD-aware evaluation.

title: Value-Preserving Architectures for Agentic AI Systems
comment: Accepted to AgenticDev Workshop at ASE 2026
summary: The emergence of agentic AI and LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) presents unprecedented opportunities for automating complex tasks, while simultaneously raising critical concerns about the preservation of fundamental human-centered values, such as privacy, fairness, and safety. Although software engineering has traditionally focused on functional correctness, the adoption of LLMs and AI agents into complex socio-technical systems has intensified the need for responsible software engineering and robust value alignment. In MAS, architectural design decisions, such as coordination mechanisms, communication protocols, and system topologies, play a central role in shaping system behavior and the outcomes they produce. This paper argues that architectural choices influence not only the functionality and performance of MAS but can also promote value-oriented system behavior. Therefore, we investigate how different architectural designs support different human-centered values, discussing the following value-preserving architectural patterns: (i) a privacy-aware architecture with a federated topology, (ii) a distributed architecture to promote pluralism and diversity, and (iii) a guard-agent architecture to detect and mitigate unfairness. Finally, we introduce representative use cases to illustrate the proposed architectures in real-world scenarios. By linking architectural design with human-centered values, this work lays the foundation for a unified set of architectural patterns and guidelines towards the design of trustworthy MAS.

AI.tldr: This paper examines how architectural design choices in LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) can be leveraged to preserve human-centered values (privacy, fairness, safety). It proposes three value-preserving architectural patterns: federated topology for privacy, distributed architecture for diversity, and guard-agent architecture for fairness detection.
AI.motivation: The emergence of agentic AI and LLM-based MAS automates complex tasks but raises critical concerns about preserving fundamental human-centered values. Traditional software engineering focuses on functional correctness, but integrating LLMs into socio-technical systems demands responsible engineering and value alignment.
AI.method: The paper investigates how different architectural designs (coordination mechanisms, communication protocols, system topologies) support different human-centered values. It proposes three value-preserving architectural patterns: (i) privacy-aware federated topology, (ii) distributed architecture for pluralism/diversity, and (iii) guard-agent architecture for unfairness detection/mitigation.
AI.result: The paper establishes a foundation for a unified set of architectural patterns and guidelines for designing trustworthy MAS by linking architectural design with human-centered values.
AI.conclusion: Architectural choices in MAS influence not only functionality and performance but also promote value-oriented system behavior. This work provides representative use cases and lays the groundwork for designing trustworthy MAS through value-preserving architectural patterns.

title: PL-SCEA: Reconfiguring Pretrained Attention for Few-Shot Industrial Anomaly Detection
summary: Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) provide transferable patch representations for few-shot industrial anomaly detection, but their attention computation is typically inherited from pretraining objectives centered on semantic aggregation. This creates a potential mismatch: token relations that support semantic recognition may not adequately expose the localized texture and structural deviations required for anomaly localization. We therefore investigate the hypothesis that the attention computation of a frozen VFM can be reconfigured as a task-relevant component of anomaly detection. We instantiate this idea with Power-Law Self-Correlation Enhanced Attention (PL-SCEA), which retains the semantic context of pretrained query-key attention while constructing token-adaptive self-correlations over contextualized value features. Positive-correlation filtering and power-law reweighting then emphasize relations that are salient relative to each token's relational background, without introducing additional trainable attention projections. The resulting features are modeled by a lightweight variational autoencoder that provides a fixed-size reconstruction-based representation of category-specific normality. The two stages serve complementary roles: attention reconfiguration shapes how local relational deviations are represented, while reconstruction-based modeling converts deviations from learned normality into anomaly scores. Across MVTec AD and VisA, the complete framework achieves competitive image-level detection and consistently strong pixel-level localization across the evaluated few-shot settings. Ablations further show that PL-SCEA improves localization with either the VAE or a memory bank under the tested setting. These results support the view that task-aligned attention reconfiguration can improve the anomaly-localization capability of frozen pretrained representations.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes PL-SCEA (Power-Law Self-Correlation Enhanced Attention), a method to reconfigure the attention mechanism of frozen Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) for few-shot industrial anomaly detection. It combines attention reconfiguration with a VAE-based reconstruction approach to achieve strong pixel-level localization while maintaining competitive image-level detection on MVTec AD and VisA datasets.
AI.motivation: The core problem is that pretrained VFMs use attention mechanisms designed for semantic aggregation, which may not effectively capture localized texture and structural deviations needed for anomaly localization. The authors hypothesize that attention computation can be reconfigured as a task-relevant component for anomaly detection without additional trainable attention projections.
AI.method: The proposed PL-SCEA retains semantic context from pretrained query-key attention while constructing token-adaptive self-correlations over contextualized value features. Key innovations include: (1) Positive-correlation filtering to emphasize salient relations relative to each token's relational background, and (2) Power-law reweighting to further enhance discriminative features. The resulting features are modeled by a lightweight variational autoencoder (VAE) to provide reconstruction-based anomaly scores. The two-stage approach combines attention reconfiguration with reconstruction-based modeling.
AI.result: The framework achieves competitive image-level detection and consistently strong pixel-level localization across few-shot settings on MVTec AD and VisA datasets. Ablations demonstrate that PL-SCEA improves localization when combined with either the VAE or a memory bank, supporting the hypothesis that task-aligned attention reconfiguration enhances anomaly-localization capability of frozen pretrained representations.
AI.conclusion: The work demonstrates that reconfiguring frozen VFM attention for task-specific (anomaly detection) objectives can significantly improve localization performance without requiring additional trainable attention projections. This supports the broader view that pretrained models can be adapted for industrial anomaly detection through strategic attention modification rather than full fine-tuning.

title: Spectral characteristics of autoencoder parameters as a vector representation of data
comment: 13 pages, 6 figures. This is a shortened (theorem proofs are skipped) and translated version of the paper published in a Russian-language peer-reviewed journal, the citation is in the paper footnote
summary: This paper examines the relationship between the parameters of autoencoder models and the statistical properties of the data on which they are trained. Autoencoders are defined as models with an encoder-decoder architecture, trained to reconstruct input data through a compressed latent representation. It is proposed that the model parameters can be viewed as a dense vector representation of the corresponding sample. To test this hypothesis, a theoretical and experimental study is conducted in which a vector representation is formed based on the spectral characteristics of the autoencoder parameter matrices. Theoretical analysis shows that the singular values of the model parameter matrices are related to the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix of the training data, ensuring the transfer of information between the data space and the parameter space. Experimental results on the CIFAR-10 and FashionMNIST datasets confirm that the resulting vector representations allow for a high degree of accuracy in distinguishing between models trained on different data subsets, without resorting to complex vector generation algorithms or using the original samples. These results suggest that the parameters of trained autoencoders can be viewed as sample representations.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether autoencoder model parameters can serve as dense vector representations of training data samples. The authors propose that the spectral characteristics of autoencoder parameter matrices encode information about the statistical properties of the training data, specifically showing that singular values of parameter matrices relate to eigenvalues of the data covariance matrix.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to explore whether trained autoencoder parameters inherently contain information about the data they were trained on, essentially treating model parameters as sample representations without requiring complex vector generation algorithms or access to original samples.
AI.method: The approach involves: (1) Theoretical analysis linking singular values of model parameter matrices to eigenvalues of the training data covariance matrix, and (2) Experimental validation using CIFAR-10 and FashionMNIST datasets, where model representations are used to distinguish between models trained on different data subsets.
AI.result: Experimental results demonstrate high accuracy in distinguishing between models trained on different data subsets using only the spectral characteristics (singular values) of autoencoder parameter matrices, without using complex vector generation algorithms or original samples.
AI.conclusion: The parameters of trained autoencoders can be viewed as sample representations, as the singular values of parameter matrices encode information about the statistical properties of the training data, enabling downstream tasks like model classification without direct access to training data.

title: Speak for Me: Giving LLMs the Situational Awareness to Participate in a Meeting
summary: In online meeting delegation, LLM agents fail to recognize when to speak. With no structured way to track stances, coverage, and floor, they miss the moments where they should contribute. Prompt-only delegates stay silent on 51.4% of the absent participant's talking opportunities on the AMI corpus. We present CAPA (Collaborative Agent Predictive Architecture), an architecture for online meeting delegation. A Perceiver updates the meeting state from each observed turn. A Predictor forecasts how the conversation will continue. A Controller decides whether to speak and which proposition to surface. A Generator phrases the chosen contribution in the participant's style. Two judges score the forecast and the action against the next observed turn. A Recalibrator updates the meeting state from those verdicts for future decisions. To evaluate online delegation, we introduce an episode-level protocol that scores whether, when, and what a delegate contributes around the participant's actual idea units. The protocol's schema-constrained LLM judges align with human annotations at Cohen's kappa = 0.71. On 137 AMI meetings, CAPA reduces the silence rate from 51.4% to 2.5%, doubles credited recovery (26.1 --> 52.2), and keeps hallucination at 0.6%. The failure mode shifts from omission to selection, with each residual near-miss attributable to a specific module of the architecture. Mechanism ablations identify the meeting state as the lever that closes the recognition gap, where raw-context scaling alone does not.

AI.tldr: CAPA (Collaborative Agent Predictive Architecture) is proposed to solve the problem of LLM agents failing to recognize when to speak in online meeting delegation. The architecture uses a Perceiver-Predictor-Controller-Generator pipeline with a Recalibrator for continuous state updates. On 137 AMI meetings, CAPA reduces silence rate from 51.4% to 2.5% and doubles credited recovery while maintaining 0.6% hallucination rate.
AI.motivation: LLM agents fail to recognize when to speak in online meeting delegation. Without a structured way to track stances, coverage, and floor, they miss moments where they should contribute. Prompt-only delegates stay silent on 51.4% of the absent participant's talking opportunities on the AMI corpus.
AI.method: CAPA consists of four main modules: (1) Perceiver updates meeting state from each observed turn; (2) Predictor forecasts how conversation will continue; (3) Controller decides whether to speak and which proposition to surface; (4) Generator phrases the contribution in the participant's style. Two judges score the forecast and action against the next observed turn. A Recalibrator updates meeting state from those verdicts for future decisions. Evaluation uses an episode-level protocol scoring whether, when, and what a delegate contributes, with schema-constrained LLM judges aligned with human annotations (Cohen's kappa = 0.71).
AI.result: On 137 AMI meetings, CAPA reduces silence rate from 51.4% to 2.5%, doubles credited recovery (26.1 → 52.2), and keeps hallucination at 0.6%. The failure mode shifts from omission to selection, with each residual near-miss attributable to a specific module. Mechanism ablations identify the meeting state as the key lever that closes the recognition gap, where raw-context scaling alone does not.
AI.conclusion: CAPA effectively addresses the speaking opportunity recognition problem in online meeting delegation. The meeting state tracking mechanism is critical for performance, while raw-context scaling provides insufficient improvement. The architecture shifts failure modes from omission to selection, making residual errors attributable to specific modules for targeted debugging.

title: Rethinking 3D Noise: Learning 3D-Aware Video Priors via Optimization-Free Morphological Perturbations
summary: 3D scene representations like NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) suffer severe artifacts in sparse-view settings. Recent generative 3D artifact fixers attempt to address this, but rely on paired corrupted and clean renders requiring costly, per-scene reconstructions across varying view configurations. While 2D image augmentations act as instant regularizers, no explicit equivalents exist for 3D representations to preserve spatial consistency across views, an essential property for 3D-aware training. We propose 3D Morphological Perturbations as an optimization-free regularizer that preserves spatial consistency. Leveraging explicit 3DGS, we treat each Gaussian as a fundamental building block - analogous to a 2D pixel - and apply perturbations across its morphological parameter space via scale, rotation, and pruning. Our method eliminates per-scene 3DGS optimization loops from dataset curation while enabling models to learn stronger geometric priors than sparse-view baselines in diagnostic ablations conducted on a lightweight video diffusion sandbox. Scaled to a 14B-parameter video model via ControlNet, our approach maintains visual fidelity while reducing mean depth error by 12.5% over state-of-the-art image-to-image 3D artifact refiners, ultimately boosting downstream robotics policy success rates by up to 8.0% across 3 of 4 manipulation tasks.

AI.tldr: 3D Morphological Perturbations (3DMP) is proposed as an optimization-free regularizer for 3D scene representations (NeRF, 3DGS) in sparse-view settings. It treats each Gaussian in 3DGS as a fundamental building block and applies perturbations via scale, rotation, and pruning to preserve spatial consistency without costly per-scene reconstructions.
AI.motivation: Current generative 3D artifact fixers require paired corrupted and clean renders with costly per-scene reconstructions across varying view configurations. While 2D image augmentations act as regularizers, no explicit equivalents exist for 3D representations to preserve spatial consistency across views, which is essential for 3D-aware training.
AI.method: The method proposes 3D Morphological Perturbations - an optimization-free regularizer leveraging explicit 3D Gaussian Splatting. Each Gaussian is treated as a fundamental building block (analogous to 2D pixels), and perturbations are applied across its morphological parameter space via scale, rotation, and pruning operations.
AI.result: The approach eliminates per-scene 3DGS optimization loops from dataset curation while enabling models to learn stronger geometric priors than sparse-view baselines. Scaled to a 14B-parameter video model via ControlNet, it maintains visual fidelity while reducing mean depth error by 12.5% over state-of-the-art image-to-image 3D artifact refiners.
AI.conclusion: 3D Morphological Perturbations successfully addresses sparse-view 3D representation artifacts. It achieves a 12.5% reduction in mean depth error compared to state-of-the-art methods and boosts downstream robotics policy success rates by up to 8.0% across 3 of 4 manipulation tasks, demonstrating practical value in robotics applications.

title: Restricted Eigenvalues Beyond Gaussian Width: Threshold Occupancy under Heavy Tails
summary: Restricted eigenvalue (RE) bounds govern stable recovery by norm-regularized estimators. For isotropic sub-Gaussian measurements, the benchmark sample size is $1+w(A)^2$, where $w(A)$ is the Gaussian width of the normalized descent cone. The COLT 2015 open-problem note (Banerjee et al., 2015) asked whether the same law follows for heavy-tailed designs from a uniform small-ball condition alone. We give an explicit and systematic negative answer to the general question as formulated there: the proposed law fails in its full dimension-free, arbitrary-set form, and the missing obstruction is simultaneous threshold occupancy. A constant-width polyhedral descent cone with fixed small-ball constants has zero empirical RE on every sample path up to half the ambient dimension. More generally, every finite range space admits exact threshold encoding in an arbitrarily narrow spherical cap and a lift to a full polyhedral descent-cone section. For every fixed threshold VC dimension $d$, as $β\downarrow0$, the sharp worst-case sample complexity is $Θ(β^{-1}[d\log(1/β)+\log(1/δ)])$. The separation persists under exact isotropy and all finite moments: on the same constant-width cone, Gaussian measurements succeed with $O(1+\log(1/δ))$ samples, whereas an isotropic heavy-tailed design fails pathwise for $n\lesssim\sqrt{p/\log p}$. Gaussian smoothing yields an everywhere-positive $C^\infty$ density while retaining arbitrarily poor RE. Under isotropy, a distribution-free fallback governed by affine dimension times squared enclosing radius is sharp on this family.

AI.tldr: This paper resolves a COLT 2015 open problem by showing that the sample complexity law for isotropic sub-Gaussian measurements (1 + w(A)²) fails for heavy-tailed designs under the uniform small-ball condition alone. The obstruction is "simultaneous threshold occupancy," and the sharp worst-case sample complexity is Θ(β⁻¹[d log(1/β) + log(1/δ)]).
AI.motivation: The COLT 2015 open problem asked whether the same sample complexity law (1 + w(A)²) that applies to isotropic sub-Gaussian measurements would also hold for heavy-tailed designs using only a uniform small-ball condition. This is a fundamental question in compressed sensing and high-dimensional statistics about the minimal assumptions needed for stable recovery.
AI.method: The authors provide a systematic negative answer through: (1) constructing constant-width polyhedral descent cones with fixed small-ball constants that have zero empirical RE on every sample path up to half the ambient dimension; (2) showing every finite range space admits exact threshold encoding in an arbitrarily narrow spherical cap with lift to full polyhedral descent-cone section; (3) analyzing the threshold VC dimension d; (4) comparing Gaussian vs heavy-tailed designs under isotropy and all finite moments.
AI.result: The proposed law fails in its full dimension-free, arbitrary-set form. For fixed threshold VC dimension d, as β↓0, the sharp worst-case sample complexity is Θ(β⁻¹[d log(1/β) + log(1/δ)]). On the same constant-width cone: Gaussian measurements succeed with O(1 + log(1/δ)) samples, while isotropic heavy-tailed designs fail pathwise for n ≲ √(p/log p). Gaussian smoothing retains arbitrarily poor RE despite yielding everywhere-positive C^∞ density. Under isotropy, a distribution-free fallback governed by affine dimension × squared enclosing radius is sharp on this family.
AI.conclusion: The sample complexity law for sub-Gaussian designs does not generalize to heavy-tailed designs under small-ball conditions alone. The key obstruction is simultaneous threshold occupancy.
