However, existing QAT methods suffer from a distinctive challenge in VDMs: while they often preserve prompt semantics, global layout, and coarse motion, the quantized model severely degrades visual details, texture fidelity, and sharpness. In this paper, we trace this degradation to the timestep-agnostic design of conventional quantization pipelines, which overlooks the stage-wise functionality of video denoising. In VDMs, early denoising steps mainly establish global structure and motion, whereas middle and late steps refine local appearance and high-frequency details. Based on this insight, we propose DSAQuant, a Denoising-Stage-Aligned Quantization-aware training framework for VDMs. During training, Denoising-Stage Oriented Supervision preserves teacher distillation in early steps for stable structure planning, while shifting later steps toward target-driven optimization to enhance detail reconstruction. During inference, Denoising-Stage Gated Guidance disables CFG in the final denoising steps to prevent it from amplifying quantization-induced errors into high-frequency artifacts. Extensive experiments on the Wan and CogVideoX families under W4A4 and W3A3 settings show that DSAQuant consistently outperforms the SOTA QAT baseline, improving the VBench average score by up to 6.60 under aggressive W3A3 quantization while preserving strong text-video alignment. These results demonstrate that effective VDM quantization requires not only reducing quantization error, but also aligning quantization training and inference with the stage-wise nature of video diffusion.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the challenge of quantizing video diffusion models (VDMs) for efficient deployment. Existing quantization-aware training methods cause severe degradation in visual details, texture fidelity, and sharpness. The authors identify the root cause as timestep-agnostic design that ignores the stage-wise nature of video denoising (early steps establish global structure, while middle/late steps refine local appearance and high-frequency details). They propose DSAQuant, a Denoising-Stage-Aligned QAT framework with two key mechanisms: Denoising-Stage Oriented Supervision for training and Denoising-Stage Gated Guidance for inference. Experiments on Wan and CogVideoX families show up to 6.60 improvement in VBench average score under W3A3 quantization.
AI.motivation: Video diffusion models (VDMs) have achieved impressive progress in text-to-video generation, but their high memory and computational costs hinder practical deployment. While quantization-aware training (QAT) is an effective compression solution, existing methods suffer from a distinctive challenge: they preserve prompt semantics, global layout, and coarse motion, but severely degrade visual details, texture fidelity, and sharpness.
AI.method: The authors propose DSAQuant, a Denoising-Stage-Aligned Quantization-aware training framework for VDMs with two key components: (1) Denoising-Stage Oriented Supervision - during training, preserves teacher distillation in early denoising steps for stable structure planning, while shifting later steps toward target-driven optimization to enhance detail reconstruction; (2) Denoising-Stage Gated Guidance - during inference, disables Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) in the final denoising steps to prevent it from amplifying quantization-induced errors into high-frequency artifacts.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on the Wan and CogVideoX families under W4A4 and W3A3 quantization settings show that DSAQuant consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art QAT baseline. It improves the VBench average score by up to 6.60 under aggressive W3A3 quantization while preserving strong text-video alignment.
AI.conclusion: Effective VDM quantization requires not only reducing quantization error, but also aligning quantization training and inference with the stage-wise nature of video diffusion. The proposed DSAQuant framework successfully addresses the degradation in visual details by leveraging the insight that early denoising steps mainly establish global structure and motion, whereas middle and late steps refine local appearance and high-frequency details.

title: Constant regret in general games via higher-order optimism
summary: We introduce an uncoupled learning algorithm which, when employed by all players of an arbitrary $N$-player normal form game with up to $K$ actions per player, guarantees $O(N^3\log^2 K)$ individual regret, uniformly over the horizon of play. The proposed algorithm - which we call higher-order optimism with discounting (HOOD) is a variant of optimistic follow-the-regularized-leader (OptFTRL) that combines a discounted $(N+1)$-th order predictor with entropic regularization over a suitable "lifting" of the game's strategy space. This combination of ingredients is purposefully designed to dampen large oscillations of the induced sequence of play in a controlled manner, removing in this way a key stumbling block of previous attempts to achieve constant regret in general games. Our approach bears several striking similarities to the concurrent - and completely independent - work of Liu, Farina, and Ozdaglar (arXiv:2608.31166), who very recently derived an $O(N^{21}\log^{4} K)$ regret bound through the use of higher-order optimism and an exponential moving average estimator.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces HOOD (Higher-Order Optimism with Discounting), an uncoupled learning algorithm for N-player normal form games that achieves O(N³log²K) individual regret. It combines discounted (N+1)-th order predictors with entropic regularization over a lifted strategy space to dampen oscillations in play.
AI.motivation: Address the challenge of achieving constant regret in general N-player games. Previous attempts were hindered by large oscillations in the induced sequence of play. The goal is to develop an uncoupled learning algorithm (where each player only knows their own payoff) that guarantees low regret uniformly over the horizon of play.
AI.method: The algorithm is a variant of Optimistic Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (OptFTRL) that combines two key ingredients: (1) a discounted (N+1)-th order predictor for better extrapolation, and (2) entropic regularization over a suitable "lifting" of the game's strategy space. This combination is designed to dampen large oscillations in a controlled manner.
AI.result: The proposed HOOD algorithm guarantees O(N³log²K) individual regret, uniformly over the horizon of play, for arbitrary N-player normal form games with up to K actions per player. This significantly improves upon the concurrent work of Liu, Farina, and Ozdaglar who achieved O(N²¹log⁴K) regret.
AI.conclusion: The paper presents a novel algorithm that overcomes previous limitations in achieving constant regret in general games. The approach achieves substantially better regret bounds (O(N³log²K) vs O(N²¹log⁴K)) compared to independent concurrent work, while addressing the oscillation problem through the combination of higher-order optimism and entropic regularization.

title: Editable Visual Design
summary:
While diffusion base models such as GPT-Image-2 and Nano-Banana exhibit remarkable visual expressiveness, their end-to-end generation inherently yields flattened bitmaps with error-prone text, precluding layer-wise post-editing. Conversely, code-based visual generation via Coding Agents provides precise layout control and decoupled layers, yet remains constrained by a lack of global aesthetic intuition and the difficulty of coding complex visual assets.
  To address this, we propose Editable Visual Design, a new paradigm driven by a Coding Agent. We designate the VLM as the ``creative brain'' for requirement comprehension, task planning, and aesthetic judgment, while utilizing the image generation model as an on-demand ``visual world simulator'' to synthesize standalone visual assets. Operating under an ``imagine first, then act'' closed-loop workflow, the agent generates isolated assets, writes native HTML/CSS, and iteratively refines the design against visual rendering feedback.
  Furthermore, Agent Design Replay faithfully reproduces the creative and reasoning trajectory akin to that of professional human designers. Ultimately, the system delivers editable artifacts with decoupled layers and real text, enabling users to perform intuitive mouse dragging and layout adjustments on a graphical user interface. Validations on posters, infographics, and other scenarios show that this paradigm successfully achieves both refined aesthetics and production-grade editability.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes "Editable Visual Design," a new paradigm combining a Vision Language Model (VLM) as creative brain with image generation models as visual simulators. Using an "imagine first, then act" closed-loop workflow, the system generates isolated visual assets, writes HTML/CSS, and iteratively refines designs. It delivers editable artifacts with decoupled layers and real text, validated on posters and infographics.
AI.motivation: Diffusion-based models (e.g., GPT-Image-2, Nano-Banana) produce flattened bitmaps with error-prone text, precluding layer-wise post-editing. Code-based visual generation via Coding Agents provides precise layout control but lacks global aesthetic intuition and struggles with complex visual assets. This work aims to bridge the gap between visual quality and editability.
AI.method: The proposed paradigm uses a VLM as the "creative brain" for requirement comprehension, task planning, and aesthetic judgment, while leveraging image generation models as "visual world simulators" to synthesize standalone visual assets. Operating under an "imagine first, then act" closed-loop workflow, the agent generates isolated assets, writes native HTML/CSS, and iteratively refines against visual rendering feedback. Additionally, "Agent Design Replay" reproduces the creative reasoning trajectory of professional designers.
AI.result: The system delivers editable artifacts with decoupled layers and real text, enabling intuitive mouse dragging and layout adjustments on a graphical user interface. Validations on posters, infographics, and other scenarios demonstrate successful achievement of both refined aesthetics and production-grade editability.
AI.conclusion: The Editable Visual Design paradigm successfully combines the visual expressiveness of diffusion models with the precise layout control of code-based generation, achieving a balance between refined aesthetics and production-grade editability for professional design applications.

title: Prospective Coding Improves Learning in Deep Continuous-Time Recurrent Networks
summary: Temporal integration gives continuous-time recurrent networks memory, but in deep stacks it also delays bottom-up signals and attenuates top-down errors. We develop Recursive Quadrature Filters (RQFs), biologically motivated complex-valued temporal filters that are a special case of diagonal state-space models (SSMs), and ask whether this failure mode can be addressed by making each layer's bottom-up input prospective. Starting from an energy model, we derive the RQF dynamics and show that each RQF is a band-pass filter whose learnable parameters control its tuning frequency and bandwidth. We then make each layer's bottom-up input prospective using a parameter-free two-tap update that leaves the recurrent transition and parallel scan unchanged. We extend this correction to general diagonal SSMs and show that it mitigates depth-dependent gradient attenuation when temporal gradients are truncated, i.e., spatial-only backpropagation. We evaluate the intervention in RQFs, S5, and ORGaNICs (a nonlinear gated RNN) trained using full backpropagation through time (BPTT) and spatial-only backpropagation. Under full BPTT, prospective variants match or outperform their non-prospective controls in every model and configuration. A non-residual width-32 six-layer RQF reaches 96.09% accuracy on raw-audio Speech Commands with 31.9k parameters; a width-64 six-layer RQF reaches 83.56% on the 16,384-step Path-X task. These results identify RQFs as a parameter-efficient recurrent substrate and prospective-input coding as an input-side correction for deep continuous-time recurrent networks.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses a fundamental problem in deep continuous-time recurrent networks where temporal integration delays bottom-up signals and attenuates top-down errors. The authors propose Recursive Quadrature Filters (RQFs), complex-valued temporal filters that are band-pass filters with learnable tuning frequency and bandwidth. They introduce a "prospective input" modification that makes each layer's bottom-up input predictive rather than reactive, without adding parameters. This approach mitigates depth-dependent gradient attenuation in spatial-only backpropagation. RQFs achieve strong results on Speech Commands (96.09% with 31.9k params) and Path-X (83.56% with width-64) benchmarks.
AI.motivation: The core problem is that temporal integration gives continuous-time recurrent networks memory, but in deep stacks this delays bottom-up signals and attenuates top-down errors. This creates a fundamental trade-off between memory (temporal integration) and gradient flow in deep architectures. The authors investigate whether making each layer's bottom-up input "prospective" (predictive) can address this failure mode.
AI.method: The authors derive RQF dynamics from an energy model, showing each RQF is a band-pass filter with learnable parameters controlling tuning frequency and bandwidth. They implement a parameter-free two-tap update to make bottom-up inputs prospective, leaving recurrent transitions and parallel scan unchanged. This is extended to general diagonal state-space models (SSMs). Evaluation is done on RQFs, S5, and ORGaNICs using both full BPTT and spatial-only backpropagation.
AI.result: Under full BPTT, prospective variants match or outperform non-prospective controls in every model and configuration. A non-residual width-32 six-layer RQF achieves 96.09% accuracy on raw-audio Speech Commands with only 31.9k parameters. A width-64 six-layer RQF achieves 83.56% on the challenging 16,384-step Path-X task.
AI.conclusion: RQFs serve as a parameter-efficient recurrent substrate, and prospective-input coding provides an effective input-side correction for deep continuous-time recurrent networks. The approach addresses the depth-dependent gradient attenuation problem, particularly when temporal gradients are truncated (spatial-only backpropagation).

title: Continuous Actions from Discrete Minds: Latent-Aligned Planning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: Bridging the gap between the discrete reasoning of Vision-Language Models and the continuous, physics-constrained nature of autonomous driving remains a significant challenge. In this work, we introduce LaPla, a unified Vision-Language-Action (VLA) framework featuring latent-aligned planning to seamlessly ground semantic understanding in precise motion execution. We first design an action tokenizer based on a residual vector-quantized variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE), capturing vehicle kinematics and encoding trajectory features into a structured latent space. Rather than discrete codebook lookups that inevitably introduce quantization errors, LaPla repurposes this representation as a physical prior to bridge the modality gap between high-dimensional semantics and the raw action space. Specifically, given multimodal inputs integrating multi-view images, historical actions, and textual instructions, LaPla incorporates concurrent action queries to causally attend to the multimodal context in a single forward pass, projecting hidden states directly into the pretrained VQ-VAE latent space. The frozen decoder then translates these continuous latents into actions, effectively eliminating quantization errors and ensuring physically plausible trajectories while bypassing time-consuming autoregressive generation. Extensive experiments on the nuScenes benchmark demonstrate that LaPla achieves competitive open-loop performance, reducing long-horizon L2 error by 15.52% compared to state-of-the-art VLA methods. Closed-loop evaluations on the NVIDIA AlpaSim simulator further confirm its superior capability in ensuring smooth driving progress, improving the success rate by 33.34 percentage points with significantly reduced inference latency.

AI.tldr: LaPla is a unified VLA framework for autonomous driving that uses latent-aligned planning to bridge semantic understanding with physics-constrained motion execution. It employs a residual VQ-VAE action tokenizer and projects hidden states directly into the pretrained latent space, eliminating quantization errors. The method achieves 15.52% L2 error reduction on nuScenes and 33.34 percentage point success rate improvement on AlpaSim simulator.
AI.motivation: The core challenge is bridging the gap between the discrete reasoning capabilities of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and the continuous, physics-constrained nature of autonomous driving. VLMs excel at semantic understanding but struggle with precise motion execution required for driving tasks.
AI.method: LaPla introduces a unified Vision-Language-Action (VLA) framework with latent-aligned planning. Key innovations include: (1) An action tokenizer based on residual VQ-VAE that captures vehicle kinematics and encodes trajectory features into a structured latent space; (2) Using the VQ-VAE representation as a physical prior to bridge the modality gap between high-dimensional semantics and raw action space; (3) Concurrent action queries that allow causal attention to multimodal context (multi-view images, historical actions, textual instructions) in a single forward pass; (4) Projecting hidden states directly into the pretrained VQ-VAE latent space, with a frozen decoder translating continuous latents into actions, eliminating quantization errors and avoiding autoregressive generation.
AI.result: Experiments on nuScenes benchmark show competitive open-loop performance with a 15.52% reduction in long-horizon L2 error compared to state-of-the-art VLA methods. Closed-loop evaluations on NVIDIA AlpaSim simulator demonstrate a 33.34 percentage point improvement in success rate with significantly reduced inference latency.
AI.conclusion: LaPla successfully bridges semantic understanding with precise motion execution through latent-aligned planning, achieving superior performance in both open-loop and closed-loop autonomous driving scenarios while maintaining computational efficiency.

title: A Low-Cost, Open Platform for End-to-End Autonomous Driving on a Miniature Ackermann Vehicle
summary: This paper presents a low-cost, open experimental platform for research in end-to-end autonomous driving with miniature Ackermann vehicles. The platform combines a physical vehicle, a printed urban track, data collection tools, trajectory registration, and a Webots digital twin, enabling controlled experiments that connect simulation-based autonomous-driving methods to real-world execution. As a first baseline, we implement command-conditioned behavior cloning, in which a neural policy receives an on-board camera image and a high-level navigation command and outputs steering and speed. The system is evaluated both on the physical vehicle and in simulation. In real closed-loop experiments, the learned policy follows lanes and executes commanded turns, reaching a mean cross-track error of 6.1 cm with respect to the reference route, close to the 4.7 cm observed in human demonstrations. In the digital twin, camera field of view has a strong effect on performance, reducing the mean cross-track error from 35.6 to 3.3 cm when widened from 58 to 120 degrees. Using the digital twin to generate synthetic driving data and a learned sim-to-real image translator to reduce the appearance gap, we further show that a higher-capacity policy trained on this synthetic data combined with real demonstrations is the only configuration that completes all four track routes in closed loop, whereas the compact baseline and the same network trained on real data alone complete fewer. These results establish the open platform as a practical testbed for sim-to-real studies and provide an initial command-conditioned imitation-learning baseline; we release it to support reproducible research.

AI.tldr: A low-cost open experimental platform for end-to-end autonomous driving using miniature Ackermann vehicles, combining physical and simulation (Webots digital twin) components. Implements command-conditioned behavior cloning as baseline. Achieves 6.1 cm mean cross-track error in real experiments, and demonstrates that synthetic data + sim-to-real translation enables completing all track routes.
AI.motivation: The gap between simulation-based autonomous driving methods and real-world execution lacks a practical testbed. Existing platforms are expensive or complex, limiting reproducibility. The authors create an accessible experimental platform to bridge sim-to-real transfer and provide a baseline for command-conditioned imitation learning.
AI.method: 1) Build a low-cost miniature Ackermann vehicle with on-board camera; 2) Create printed urban track with trajectory registration; 3) Develop Webots digital twin; 4) Implement command-conditioned behavior cloning (neural policy: camera image + navigation command → steering/speed); 5) Use learned sim-to-real image translator to reduce appearance gap between synthetic and real images.
AI.result: Real closed-loop experiments: mean cross-track error 6.1 cm (vs 4.7 cm human demonstration). Digital twin: widening FOV from 58° to 120° reduces error from 35.6 cm to 3.3 cm. Only the policy trained on synthetic data + real demonstrations with sim-to-real translation completes all four track routes.
AI.conclusion: The platform serves as a practical testbed for sim-to-real studies. The command-conditioned behavior cloning baseline achieves close-to-human performance. Synthetic data generation combined with learned sim-to-real adaptation is essential for full route completion, demonstrating the platform's value for reproducible autonomous driving research.

title: TAP-Path: Task-Adaptive Structural and Token Pruning for Efficient and Trustworthy Pathology Foundation Models
summary: Pathology foundation models improve transferable representation learning for histopathology, but recent gains often rely on encoders with hundreds of millions of parameters and high inference cost. We propose TAP-Path, a task-adaptive compression framework that directly restructures a pretrained Virchow2 encoder rather than distilling it into a separate student. TAP-Path combines validation-driven transformer-block selection, physical removal of redundant blocks, input-adaptive patch-token pruning, multi-depth feature recovery, and a lightweight gated task head. The final model retains 24 of 32 transformer blocks and 70% of patch tokens after pruning, reducing encoder parameters by 24.96% (631.24M to 473.70M) and analytical encoder compute by 35.20% (340.13G to 220.40G FLOPs). Across three task-head optimization seeds, TAP-Path achieved $87.98 \pm 0.067%$ test accuracy, $81.26 \pm 0.49%$ balanced accuracy, and $82.38 \pm 0.48%$ macro-F1 on a 32-class histopathology benchmark, compared with 86.89% for full Virchow2 and 87.67% for UNI2-h. TAP-Path achieved a Brier score of $0.1800 \pm 0.0005$ and failure-detection AUROC of $0.9047 \pm 0.0060$. A validation-only rare-aware objective improved rare-class balanced accuracy in a secondary operating analysis. Frozen external evaluation on 433 CPTAC samples yielded $91.22 \pm 0.83%$ accuracy and $91.10 \pm 0.81%$ balanced accuracy. These results show that task-adaptive structural and token sparsification can improve the accuracy-efficiency trade-off of large pathology foundation models while preserving reliability under internal and external evaluation.

AI.tldr: TAP-Path is a task-adaptive compression framework that reduces a large pathology foundation model (Virchow2) by 24.96% in parameters and 35.20% in compute while slightly improving accuracy on a 32-class histopathology benchmark, achieving 87.98% test accuracy and strong reliability metrics.
AI.motivation: Large pathology foundation models like Virchow2 achieve state-of-the-art performance but require hundreds of millions of parameters and high inference cost, making them impractical for deployment. The authors sought to improve the accuracy-efficiency trade-off through task-adaptive structural compression.
AI.method: TAP-Path directly restructures the pretrained Virchow2 encoder through: (1) validation-driven transformer-block selection to identify redundant blocks, (2) physical removal of selected blocks, (3) input-adaptive patch-token pruning retaining 70% of tokens, (4) multi-depth feature recovery, and (5) a lightweight gated task head. The approach was evaluated across three random seeds for task-head optimization.
AI.result: TAP-Path retained 24 of 32 transformer blocks and 70% of patch tokens, reducing encoder parameters from 631.24M to 473.70M (24.96% reduction) and FLOPs from 340.13G to 220.40G (35.20% reduction). Performance on a 32-class histopathology benchmark: 87.98 ± 0.067% test accuracy, 81.26 ± 0.49% balanced accuracy, 82.38 ± 0.48% macro-F1, outperforming full Virchow2 (86.89%) and UNI2-h (87.67%). Brier score: 0.1800 ± 0.0005; failure-detection AUROC: 0.9047 ± 0.0060. External validation on 433 CPTAC samples achieved 91.22 ± 0.83% accuracy and 91.10 ± 0.81% balanced accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Task-adaptive structural and token sparsification can improve the accuracy-efficiency trade-off of large pathology foundation models while preserving reliability under both internal and external evaluation. The compression approach not only reduces computational cost but actually improves accuracy over the full model, demonstrating that redundant parameters can be removed without performance loss.

title: Robust PAC Learning of Concurrent Stochastic Games
comment: Main text: 10 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables; Appendix: 22 pages, 2 figures, 1 table
summary: We introduce the first Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning framework for general-sum concurrent stochastic games (CSGs) with transition uncertainty, while addressing the challenge of Nash equilibrium (NE) existence. Our algorithm maintains data-driven $L^1$ confidence sets over transition kernels and solves a robust CSG to compute a social-welfare optimal $\varepsilon$-NE, using a robust MDP-based exploration mechanism to drive joint state-action coverage. Crucially, we introduce a Nash margin characterisation that enables principled reasoning about equilibrium existence: the framework either returns an $\varepsilon$-approximate NE whose social-welfare value is $\varepsilon$-close to optimal, or provides a sound certificate that no exact NE exists. Under a minimum reachability condition $p_{\mathrm{reach}}>0$ over relevant state-action pairs, the algorithm terminates after a polynomial number of trajectory samples, with sample complexity $\widetilde{O}\left( {R_{\max}^2 H^4 |S|^2 |A| / (p_{\mathrm{reach}} \varepsilon^2)} \right)$. Empirical results on benchmark CSGs demonstrate near-optimal performance, correct handling of equilibrium (non-)existence, and sample complexity consistent with theory.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning framework for general-sum concurrent stochastic games (CSGs) with transition uncertainty. The approach maintains data-driven L¹ confidence sets over transition kernels and solves a robust CSG to compute a social-welfare optimal ε-Nash equilibrium, with a mechanism to either return an ε-approximate NE or provide a certificate that no exact NE exists.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to address two key challenges in stochastic games: (1) learning in environments with transition uncertainty, and (2) the fundamental problem of Nash equilibrium (NE) existence. Existing approaches struggle with these issues, particularly the lack of principled methods to reason about equilibrium existence while providing sample complexity guarantees.
AI.method: The method involves: (1) maintaining data-driven L¹ confidence sets over transition kernels, (2) solving a robust CSG to compute a social-welfare optimal ε-NE, (3) using a robust MDP-based exploration mechanism to drive joint state-action coverage, and (4) introducing a Nash margin characterization to reason about equilibrium existence. The algorithm requires a minimum reachability condition p_reach > 0 over relevant state-action pairs.
AI.result: Theoretical results show the algorithm terminates after a polynomial number of trajectory samples with sample complexity Ō(R_max² H⁴ |S|² |A| / (p_reach ε²)). Empirical results on benchmark CSGs demonstrate near-optimal performance, correct handling of equilibrium (non-)existence, and sample complexity consistent with theory.
AI.conclusion: This work provides the first PAC learning framework for general-sum CSGs with transition uncertainty, with a principled approach to handling NE existence through the Nash margin characterization. The framework provides strong theoretical guarantees (polynomial sample complexity) while being empirically validated on benchmark problems.

title: CORE: Improving Compositional Reasoning in MLLM Embedding via Reranker Distillation
summary: MLLM-based embedding models remain limited in compositional retrieval, often failing to distinguish scenes containing the same concepts but different attribute-object bindings. Yet the same backbone can resolve such distinctions when used as a cross-attentive reranker, motivating us to distill its compositional judgments into the embedding model. We propose CORE, which synthesizes candidate lists spanning five compositional matching levels and introduces a Rank-KL objective that trains the embedding model to reproduce the reranker's fine-grained ranking. We further introduce a graded evaluation protocol and compare contrastive learning, pairwise CoSENT, and listwise Rank-KL under the same data and tuning budget. Our comparison shows that both CoSENT and Rank-KL use the multi-level supervision more effectively than contrastive learning, with Rank-KL achieving the strongest overall performance. Across three compositional reasoning benchmarks (COLA, SUGARCREPE++, NEGBENCH), CORE-RERANKER-8B achieves an 82.7% total average, outperforming Jina-Reranker by 10.7 points, while CORE-EMBED-8B achieves the best total average (0.666) among all evaluated embedding models. The improvements transfer to the MCMR benchmark without sacrificing retrieval performance on COCO and Flickr30K.

AI.tldr: CORE distills compositional reasoning from cross-attentive rerankers into embedding models by training with a Rank-KL objective on multi-level compositional matching candidates. This approach outperforms prior methods on compositional retrieval benchmarks.
AI.motivation: MLLM-based embedding models struggle with compositional retrieval - they cannot distinguish scenes with same concepts but different attribute-object bindings. However, the same backbone can make these distinctions when used as a cross-attentive reranker, suggesting the potential to transfer this capability to embedding models.
AI.method: CORE synthesizes candidate lists across five compositional matching levels and introduces a Rank-KL objective that trains the embedding model to reproduce the reranker's fine-grained ranking. The method compares three training approaches: contrastive learning, pairwise CoSENT, and listwise Rank-KL under identical data and tuning budgets.
AI.result: Rank-KL achieves strongest overall performance. CORE-RERANKER-8B achieves 82.7% total average (+10.7 vs Jina-Reranker). CORE-EMBED-8B achieves best total average (0.666) among embedding models. Improvements transfer to MCMR benchmark without sacrificing retrieval performance on COCO and Flickr30K.
AI.conclusion: Distilling reranker's compositional judgments into embedding models via Rank-KL objective is effective. Both CoSENT and Rank-KL outperform contrastive learning with multi-level supervision, with Rank-KL achieving the best results across compositional reasoning benchmarks.

title: Efficient Semantic Understanding from Digital Foveation
comment: Accepted at the 3rd Human-inspired Computer Vision Workshop at ECCV 2026
summary: Dense semantic segmentation allocates computational resources uniformly across the entire image, regardless of scene complexity or task relevance. Inspired by biological vision, we investigate whether semantic understanding can be achieved more efficiently through digital foveated perception. We introduce a lightweight active-vision pipeline that combines saliency-driven fixation selection, high-resolution foveal observations, low-resolution contextual information, semantic accumulation, and adaptive computation. Beyond conventional dense prediction metrics, we use object-level evaluation to measure semantic understanding under sparse observations. On ADE20K-Object, a single foveated observation achieves 95.9% of the baseline Top-1 accuracy and 96.9% of the baseline Top-3 accuracy while requiring only 4.7% of the computational cost. At the scene level, semantic accumulation recovers 90.6% of the baseline object recall while using 58.6% of the computation. These results suggest that substantial semantic understanding can emerge from sparse observations when computation is allocated selectively, highlighting active vision as an efficient alternative to uniform dense processing and motivating evaluation protocols beyond conventional pixel-wise segmentation metrics.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a digital foveated perception system for efficient semantic segmentation, mimicking biological vision. By using saliency-driven fixation selection with high-resolution foveal and low-resolution peripheral observations, the method achieves 95.9% of baseline Top-1 accuracy with only 4.7% computational cost, demonstrating that sparse observations can yield substantial semantic understanding.
AI.motivation: Dense semantic segmentation wastes computational resources by processing all image regions uniformly, regardless of their relevance. The authors are inspired by biological vision systems, where the fovea provides high-resolution central vision while peripheral vision uses lower resolution. This biological principle suggests that selective, adaptive attention could achieve efficient semantic understanding.
AI.method: The authors introduce a lightweight active-vision pipeline with five key components: (1) saliency-driven fixation selection to determine where to look, (2) high-resolution foveal observations for detailed analysis, (3) low-resolution contextual information for scene context, (4) semantic accumulation to combine observations over time, and (5) adaptive computation allocation. They also propose object-level evaluation beyond conventional pixel-wise metrics.
AI.result: On ADE20K-Object dataset: (1) A single foveated observation achieves 95.9% of baseline Top-1 accuracy and 96.9% of baseline Top-3 accuracy while requiring only 4.7% of computational cost. (2) At scene level, semantic accumulation recovers 90.6% of baseline object recall while using 58.6% of computation. These results demonstrate significant efficiency gains with minimal accuracy loss.
AI.conclusion: Substantial semantic understanding can emerge from sparse observations when computation is allocated selectively based on task relevance. Active vision provides an efficient alternative to uniform dense processing. The authors also motivate the need for evaluation protocols beyond conventional pixel-wise segmentation metrics, suggesting object-level evaluation is more appropriate for assessing semantic understanding in sparse observation scenarios.

title: The Shape of Time: Video-Token Contrast for Temporal Understanding in VideoLMs
summary: Seeing frames in order does not mean representing time. Modern VideoLMs receive ordered video streams, yet their main supervision acts on generated text rather than video-token representations where event dynamics should first emerge. This mismatch allows models to learn temporal answers from shortcuts such as objects, scenes, and language priors, without requiring internal video representations to capture event progression. To address this, we propose VT-Contrast, a representation-level temporal counterfactual objective for VideoLMs. Its design asks where temporal supervision should act and what temporal differences it should expose. VT-Contrast supervises selected late-layer last-frame video tokens, where temporal information is expected to be integrated before language generation, and contrasts order-preserving views with same-video reordered counterfactuals graded by Kendall tau distance. It requires no architectural changes, is compatible with diverse VideoLM training tasks, and improves overall performance across temporal understanding benchmarks. Our code is available at https://github.com/ANDgate99/VT-Contrast.

AI.tldr: VT-Contrast is a representation-level temporal counterfactual objective for VideoLMs that supervises late-layer last-frame video tokens by contrasting order-preserving views with reordered counterfactuals, requiring no architectural changes and improving temporal understanding benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Modern VideoLMs receive ordered video streams but are supervised on generated text rather than video-token representations. This mismatch allows models to learn temporal answers from shortcuts (objects, scenes, language priors) without requiring internal video representations to capture event progression.
AI.method: VT-Contrast supervises selected late-layer last-frame video tokens (where temporal information is integrated before language generation) and contrasts order-preserving views with same-video reordered counterfactuals graded by Kendall tau distance. It requires no architectural changes and is compatible with diverse VideoLM training tasks.
AI.result: Improves overall performance across temporal understanding benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: VT-Contrast provides an effective representation-level temporal supervision approach that addresses the shortcut learning problem in VideoLMs without requiring architectural modifications, and can be integrated with various VideoLM training tasks.

title: BooM-VVT: Boosting Mask-Free Video Virtual Try-On with Image-Level Pseudo Data
comment: 23 pages, 18 figures, 8 tables. Accepted to ACM Multimedia 2026 (MM '26)
summary:
Video virtual try-on (VVT) aims to generate realistic videos of a person wearing a target garment. Recent methods leverage a keyframe-driven video generation paradigm to improve in-the-wild performance, yet they still rely on masks to localize try-on regions, making them vulnerable to large motions and severe occlusions. Although mask-free image-based try-on methods have shown promising results by leveraging large-scale pseudo data, extending this paradigm to videos remains difficult, as constructing video-level pseudo data is prohibitively expensive. Furthermore, coarse keyframe sampling and the scarcity of multi-view try-on data limit existing keyframe-driven methods in maintaining garment consistency and handling diverse try-on tasks.
  To address these challenges, we propose BooM-VVT, a mask-free VVT framework built upon the keyframe-driven paradigm. To achieve mask-free VVT, we introduce a multi-stage training strategy that leverages image-level pseudo data for mask-free localization learning, substantially reducing the need for costly video-level pseudo data. To improve garment consistency, we propose Garment-Sensitive Keyframe Sampling, which selects keyframes based on garment-relevant body regions to better capture garment appearance. We further introduce Frame-Shared 3D-RoPE to establish spatiotemporal correspondences between keyframes and target video frames for accurate garment-detail transfer. Finally, we construct OmniView, a large-scale multi-view try-on dataset to support reliable try-on video generation under complex camera viewpoints and diverse try-on tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that BooM-VVT achieves superior temporal consistency and garment fidelity over existing methods. Project page: https://boomvvt.github.io/boomvvt.

AI.tldr: BooM-VVT is a mask-free video virtual try-on framework that addresses limitations of existing methods by using multi-stage training with image-level pseudo data, garment-sensitive keyframe sampling, Frame-Shared 3D-RoPE for spatiotemporal correspondence, and a new multi-view dataset (OmniView) to achieve superior temporal consistency and garment fidelity.
AI.motivation: Existing video virtual try-on methods rely on masks for try-on region localization, making them vulnerable to large motions and occlusions. While mask-free image-based try-on exists, extending it to videos is expensive due to costly video-level pseudo data. Additionally, coarse keyframe sampling and scarcity of multi-view data limit garment consistency and handling of diverse try-on tasks.
AI.method: 1) Multi-stage training strategy using image-level pseudo data for mask-free localization learning, reducing need for expensive video-level pseudo data. 2) Garment-Sensitive Keyframe Sampling that selects keyframes based on garment-relevant body regions. 3) Frame-Shared 3D-RoPE to establish spatiotemporal correspondences between keyframes and target video frames. 4) Construction of OmniView, a large-scale multi-view try-on dataset.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate that BooM-VVT achieves superior temporal consistency and garment fidelity over existing methods.
AI.conclusion: BooM-VVT successfully enables mask-free video virtual try-on through innovative training strategies and architectural components, providing a robust solution for in-the-wild try-on videos with complex motions and occlusions.

title: Beyond Retrieval: Progressive Latent Memory Evolution for Streaming Video Understanding
summary: Streaming video understanding requires multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to process continuous visual inputs and respond to user queries under strict causality and bounded memory. Existing approaches typically compress historical observations into an external memory bank and retrieve query-relevant evidence as additional visual context. Though effective, this store-and-retrieve paradigm keeps historical evidence as external visual context, preventing it from being internalized into a compact, evolving latent memory that can continuously guide streaming reasoning. To bridge this gap, we introduce LatentStream, a progressive latent working memory framework that shifts streaming memory from store-and-retrieve to retrieve-and-internalize. Specifically, LatentStream comprises three coordinated components. First, Query-agnostic Hierarchical Streaming Memory organizes visual history into short-, mid-, and long-term levels under a fixed memory budget through Jenks-guided adaptive consolidation. Once a query arrives, Hierarchical Latent Memory Evolution equips groups of latent memory tokens with progressively expanding memory receptive fields, enabling them to iteratively retrieve historical evidence from their corresponding scopes and internalize it into a compact, fixed-length latent memory. Finally, Progressive Confidence-guided Latent Memory Optimization constructs a hierarchical progression reward from group-wise predictive entropy and jointly refines the latent memory tokens and retrieved evidence, encouraging increasingly confident streaming reasoning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LatentStream achieves new state-of-the-art results on existing online and offline video benchmarks.

AI.tldr: LatentStream introduces a progressive latent working memory framework for streaming video understanding that shifts from store-and-retrieve to retrieve-and-internalize paradigm. It uses three coordinated components: hierarchical streaming memory organization, latent memory evolution with expanding receptive fields, and confidence-guided optimization to achieve state-of-the-art results on video benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing streaming video understanding approaches use a store-and-retrieve paradigm that keeps historical evidence as external visual context, preventing it from being internalized into a compact, evolving latent memory that can continuously guide streaming reasoning. This limitation hinders efficient processing of continuous visual inputs under strict causality and bounded memory constraints.
AI.method: LatentStream comprises three coordinated components: (1) Query-agnostic Hierarchical Streaming Memory organizes visual history into short-, mid-, and long-term levels under fixed memory budget using Jenks-guided adaptive consolidation; (2) Hierarchical Latent Memory Evolution equips groups of latent memory tokens with progressively expanding memory receptive fields to iteratively retrieve and internalize historical evidence into compact fixed-length latent memory; (3) Progressive Confidence-guided Latent Memory Optimization constructs hierarchical progression reward from group-wise predictive entropy and jointly refines latent memory tokens and retrieved evidence.
AI.result: LatentStream achieves new state-of-the-art results on existing online and offline video benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: The retrieve-and-internalize paradigm with progressive latent working memory effectively addresses streaming video understanding challenges by enabling historical evidence to be internalized into compact latent memory, demonstrating superior performance over traditional store-and-retrieve approaches.

title: Persistent Identity Preservation in Generative Image Models: A Benchmark and Evaluation System
summary: Generative image models can now produce high-quality images, follow complex instructions, and support precise edits, but they still struggle to preserve who or what is being depicted. When generating or editing images of a specific subject, identity may drift as the pose, expression, appearance, viewpoint, or surrounding scene changes. Existing subject-driven methods make fundamentally different choices about where identity is represented: through the input context (GPT-Image-2, NB2), as trainable subject-specific model parameters (LoRA), or as a persistent identity layer (PHOTA IDENTITY) reusable across generations and edits. We systematically benchmark these paradigms across subject-driven generation, editing, restoration, and multi-subject settings, with tasks designed to increasingly stress identity preservation. Our results show that identity preservation remains a distinct limitation of current generative foundation models: strong image quality and instruction following do not necessarily imply strong identity fidelity, and identity degradation becomes more pronounced under iterative edits, small subject scales, severe image degradation, and multi-subject composition. Persistent identity substantially reduces this degradation across generation, editing, and restoration, consistently improving identity preservation when applied to different foundation models while maintaining comparable instruction adherence and perceptual image quality. These results suggest that identity does not simply emerge from increasingly capable generative models, but can instead be represented as persistent subject knowledge that is composed independently with the underlying generative model.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically benchmarks three paradigms for identity preservation in subject-driven image generation: input context (GPT-Image-2, NB2), trainable parameters (LoRA), and persistent identity layers (PHOTA IDENTITY). The study reveals that current generative models struggle with identity preservation under various stressors, and that persistent identity layers consistently outperform other approaches across generation, editing, and restoration tasks.
AI.motivation: Despite advances in generative image models producing high-quality images with complex instruction following, identity preservation remains a critical limitation. When generating or editing images of specific subjects, identity drifts due to changes in pose, expression, appearance, viewpoint, or surrounding context. The research aims to systematically compare different paradigms for maintaining subject identity across various challenging conditions.
AI.method: The researchers benchmarked three identity representation paradigms across multiple tasks: subject-driven generation, editing, restoration, and multi-subject settings. They designed tasks that progressively stress identity preservation, testing under conditions including iterative edits, small subject scales, severe image degradation, and multi-subject composition. They evaluated persistent identity layers applied to different foundation models while measuring instruction adherence and perceptual image quality.
AI.result: The study found that identity preservation remains a distinct limitation of current generative foundation models. Strong image quality and instruction following do not guarantee strong identity fidelity. Identity degradation becomes more pronounced under iterative edits, small subject scales, severe image degradation, and multi-subject composition. The persistent identity approach substantially reduces degradation across generation, editing, and restoration tasks while maintaining comparable instruction adherence and perceptual image quality.
AI.conclusion: The results suggest that identity does not simply emerge from increasingly capable generative models. Instead, identity can be represented as persistent subject knowledge that can be composed independently with the underlying generative model. This approach offers a promising direction for improving identity preservation in subject-driven image generation systems.

title: Zero-Shot Novel Depth Synthesis Using 3D Foundation Models Scene Representations
comment: Accepted to the European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV) 2026. Project page: https://akola-mbey-denis.github.io/Z3D-page/
summary: 3D Foundation Models (3DFMs) such as VGGT have recently pushed the boundaries of 3D vision by predicting rich unified representations with feed-foward transformers. The scene representations learned by these models enable strong performance on multiple 3D vision tasks. In this paper, we investigate using their internal representations to infer 3D in the scene from new views. Our hypothesis is that in order to solve the task of 3D reconstruction, these models need to learn a representation that includes a large amount of general knowledge about 3D scenes. After showing that it is possible to decode hidden surfaces from internal 3DFM representations, we propose a method, Z3D, that estimates pointmaps in unseen views by doing latent diffusion on 3DFM representation. We show that Z3D can predict realistic depth maps for new views across multiple datasets.

AI.tldr: This paper presents Z3D, a method that leverages internal representations of 3D Foundation Models (3DFMs) like VGGT to perform novel view synthesis. The approach decodes hidden surfaces from 3DFM internal representations and uses latent diffusion to estimate pointmaps in unseen views, demonstrating realistic depth map prediction across multiple datasets.
AI.motivation: The authors hypothesize that to solve 3D reconstruction, 3DFMs must learn representations containing general knowledge about 3D scenes. This work investigates whether these internal representations can be exploited to infer 3D structure from novel viewpoints, beyond the model's original training objectives.
AI.method:
1) Demonstrate that hidden surfaces can be decoded from internal 3DFM representations
2) Propose Z3D method that performs latent diffusion on 3DFM representations to estimate pointmaps in unseen views
3) Predict depth maps for new views across multiple datasets
AI.result: Z3D can predict realistic depth maps for new views across multiple datasets, showing that 3DFM internal representations contain sufficient 3D scene knowledge for novel view synthesis.
AI.conclusion: Internal representations of 3D Foundation Models contain rich 3D scene information that can be exploited for novel view synthesis through latent diffusion, enabling realistic depth prediction without explicit 3D reconstruction pipelines.

title: Seeing Before Synthesizing: VLM-Guided Transition Event Discovery for Weakly-Supervised Dense Video Captioning
summary: Weakly-Supervised Dense Video Captioning aims to localize and describe multiple events in untrimmed videos given only an ordered set of event-level captions per video. Recent work synthesizes auxiliary transition captions via LLM to provide additional vision-language alignment, but these captions lack visual grounding and are rigidly assigned to every inter-event gap at a fixed location and duration. To address these, we propose Seeing Before Synthesizing (SBS), a framework that adaptively provides visually grounded linguistic guidance only where warranted. Leveraging a VLM, we generate frame-level narratives for the inter-event gaps and detect transitions from the semantic variation across them. For identified transitions, we then refine inter-event temporal masks by blending the temporal midpoint with the semantic change point and selecting the width that maximizes vision-language alignment. Experiments on ActivityNet Captions and YouCook2 demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both captioning and localization.

AI.tldr: SBS is a weakly-supervised dense video captioning framework that uses a VLM to generate visually grounded narratives for inter-event gaps, adaptively detects transitions from semantic variation, and refines temporal masks by blending temporal midpoints with semantic change points to maximize vision-language alignment.
AI.motivation: Previous work synthesizes auxiliary transition captions via LLM, but these captions lack visual grounding and are rigidly assigned to every inter-event gap at fixed location and duration. SBS addresses these limitations by providing adaptive, visually grounded linguistic guidance only where warranted.
AI.method: SBS framework uses a VLM to generate frame-level narratives for inter-event gaps and detects transitions from semantic variation. For identified transitions, it refines temporal masks by blending temporal midpoint with semantic change point and selects width that maximizes vision-language alignment.
AI.result: SBS achieves state-of-the-art performance on ActivityNet Captions and YouCook2 datasets in both captioning and localization tasks.
AI.conclusion: The proposed SBS framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on ActivityNet Captions and YouCook2 datasets in both captioning and localization tasks, demonstrating the effectiveness of adaptive, visually grounded linguistic guidance for weakly-supervised dense video captioning.

title: One Editor, Many Edits: A Unified Training-Free Framework for Diverse Video Editing
summary: Video editing spans diverse editing paradigms, yet achieving high-quality instruction-guided and subject-guided editing within a single unified framework remains challenging. We introduce EditVid, a training-free framework combining sparse causal memory for local coherence, correspondence-based post-attention token injection for long-range identity preservation, and soft latent blending for edit locality. The same framework supports instruction-guided and reference-guided edits, including style transfer, attribute modification, object insertion, part-level editing, and subject replacement. On FiVE, EditVid achieves 78.16 FiVE-Acc, compared with 58.95 for the strongest evaluated training-free baseline, while obtaining competitive results on IVEBench. A user study further shows a 51.8\% overall preference for EditVid over 7 competing methods.

AI.tldr: EditVid is a training-free video editing framework that unifies instruction-guided and reference-guided editing, supporting style transfer, attribute modification, object insertion, part-level editing, and subject replacement through sparse causal memory, correspondence-based token injection, and soft latent blending.
AI.motivation: Video editing spans diverse paradigms, but achieving high-quality instruction-guided and subject-guided editing within a single unified framework remains challenging.
AI.method: EditVid combines three key techniques: (1) sparse causal memory for local coherence, (2) correspondence-based post-attention token injection for long-range identity preservation, and (3) soft latent blending for edit locality. The framework is training-free.
AI.result: On FiVE benchmark, EditVid achieves 78.16 FiVE-Acc, compared with 58.95 for the strongest evaluated training-free baseline. It also obtains competitive results on IVEBench. A user study shows 51.8% overall preference over 7 competing methods.
AI.conclusion: EditVid successfully provides a unified framework for diverse video editing tasks, achieving state-of-the-art performance among training-free methods while maintaining broad applicability across different editing paradigms.

title: Puffin-World: Scaling a Unified Multimodal Model with Native 3D World States
summary: We propose Puffin-World, a unified multimodal architecture that integrates physical understanding, spatial simulation, and 3D world generation and reconstruction without relying on external offline modules. To reliably construct and interact with 3D worlds, our framework jointly models three native world states: physics (gravity field and latitude), geometry (depth), and appearance (image), together with a unified Omni-Camera representation that supports diverse tasks and flexible motions. Beyond modeling these states, we introduce a strategy for propagating physical dynamics across future frames. By grounding absolute camera properties in the real world, Puffin-World enables physically consistent and visually stable world generation. We further couple appearance and geometry within a single generative process, jointly synthesizing each future view and reconstructing its underlying geometry. This unified paradigm enables interleaved closed-loop applications requiring synergy across multiple tasks, including mimic and self-calibrated world exploration. To scale Puffin-World to complex scenarios, we construct Puffin-16M, comprising 15 million vision-language-camera triplets and 1 million trajectories featuring various and challenging motions. To foster further research in this area, we released the code, models, and datasets.

AI.tldr: Puffin-World is a unified multimodal architecture that integrates physical understanding, spatial simulation, and 3D world generation/reconstruction without external offline modules. It jointly models physics (gravity field and latitude), geometry (depth), and appearance (image) states with an Omni-Camera representation.
AI.motivation: To reliably construct and interact with 3D worlds, there is a need for a framework that can jointly model physical dynamics, geometry, and appearance while enabling physically consistent and visually stable world generation through absolute camera properties grounded in the real world.
AI.method: The framework jointly models three native world states (physics, geometry, appearance) with a unified Omni-Camera representation. It uses a strategy for propagating physical dynamics across future frames and couples appearance and geometry within a single generative process. The model is trained on Puffin-16M dataset comprising 15 million vision-language-camera triplets and 1 million trajectories with challenging motions.
AI.result: Puffin-World enables physically consistent and visually stable world generation, supports interleaved closed-loop applications requiring synergy across multiple tasks (mimic and self-calibrated world exploration), and achieves joint synthesis of future views with underlying geometry reconstruction.
AI.conclusion: The unified paradigm successfully enables interleaved closed-loop applications requiring synergy across multiple tasks. The researchers released code, models, and datasets (Puffin-16M) to foster further research in unified physical understanding, spatial simulation, and 3D world generation.

title: Principia: Relational Physics Tests for Video Models
summary: Evaluating physical reasoning in video models is difficult because absolute motion measurements depend on frame rate, object scale, and camera calibration, all of which are often ambiguous or unavailable in generated video. We propose a different approach. When two objects in the same scene obey the same physical law, their motions must satisfy predictable relationships, and these relationships hold independent of calibration. We introduce Principia, a benchmark that evaluates Newtonian physics through relational consistency between paired objects. Principia spans eight phenomena - gravity, restitution, friction, rotational inertia, projectile motion, momentum, pendulum, and mass-spring oscillation - across translational, rotational, collisional, and oscillatory dynamics, using real-world scenes recorded under controlled protocols. We also introduce a calibration-independent consistency score that quantifies physical violation directly in image space. Across thousands of generations from six state-of-the-art video generators, no model exceeds 0.42 on Principia despite all scoring around 0.8 on VBench. Vision-language models are evaluated on their ability to detect relational physics violations, with the best model achieving only 67% accuracy and most performing near chance level.

AI.tldr: Principia is a benchmark for evaluating physical reasoning in video models through relational consistency between paired objects, independent of camera calibration. It covers 8 physical phenomena and reveals that current video generators fail at physical realism (max 0.42 score) despite performing well on VBench (0.8), and vision-language models struggle to detect physics violations (best 67% accuracy).
AI.motivation: Evaluating physical reasoning in video models is challenging because absolute motion measurements depend on frame rate, object scale, and camera calibration, which are often ambiguous or unavailable in generated video. The authors propose that when two objects obey the same physical law, their motions must satisfy predictable relationships that hold independent of calibration.
AI.method: The paper introduces Principia, a benchmark evaluating Newtonian physics through relational consistency between paired objects. It spans 8 phenomena (gravity, restitution, friction, rotational inertia, projectile motion, momentum, pendulum, mass-spring oscillation) across translational, rotational, collisional, and oscillatory dynamics using real-world scenes. A calibration-independent consistency score quantifies physical violation directly in image space.
AI.result: Across thousands of generations from six state-of-the-art video generators, no model exceeds 0.42 on Principia despite all scoring around 0.8 on VBench. Vision-language models evaluated on detecting relational physics violations achieve only 67% accuracy at best, with most performing near chance level.
AI.conclusion: Current video generation models lack physical realism - they perform well on standard quality benchmarks (VBench) but fail fundamentally at physical correctness. Additionally, vision-language models cannot reliably detect these physics violations, indicating a significant gap in both video generation and physical understanding capabilities.

title: Scal3R: Learning Efficient Multi-Relative Pose Query for Scalable Online 3D Reconstruction
summary: Online 3D reconstruction models perform poorly on long videos. This happens because regressing poses relative to a fixed first-frame anchor forces extrapolation far beyond the training distribution. Small drifts accumulate and amplify into significant geometric collapse. However, we observe that per-frame depth remains stable throughout this failure. The backbone's local geometry remains intact; only the global pose head breaks down. Motivated by this decoupling, we introduce Scal3R. This approach reformulates online reconstruction as multi-reference relative pose querying. We use lightweight learnable tokens, which make up about ~1% of the parameters, and inject them into a completely frozen backbone via asymmetric attention. This setup queries poses relative to multiple past keyframes. An online pose-graph optimization system with loop closure suppresses long-range drift. Scal3R reaches convergence in 8 hours on a single GPU. It reduces the average ATE by over 60% on KITTI compared to the online baseline. It also achieves state-of-the-art performance across Virtual KITTI, Sintel, TUM-Dynamic, ScanNet, and 7-Scenes. Project page: https://linjohnss.github.io/scal3r/

AI.tldr: Scal3R addresses long video 3D reconstruction failure by reformulating it as multi-reference relative pose querying using lightweight learnable tokens (~1% parameters) injected into a frozen backbone via asymmetric attention, combined with online pose-graph optimization for loop closure.
AI.motivation: Online 3D reconstruction models perform poorly on long videos because regressing poses relative to a fixed first-frame anchor forces extrapolation beyond training distribution, causing small drifts to accumulate into geometric collapse. However, per-frame depth remains stable, indicating only the global pose head fails while local geometry stays intact.
AI.method: Scal3R uses lightweight learnable tokens (~1% of parameters) injected into a frozen backbone via asymmetric attention to query poses relative to multiple past keyframes. An online pose-graph optimization system with loop closure suppresses long-range drift.
AI.result: Scal3R converges in 8 hours on a single GPU, reduces average ATE by over 60% on KITTI compared to the online baseline, and achieves state-of-the-art performance across Virtual KITTI, Sintel, TUM-Dynamic, ScanNet, and 7-Scenes.
AI.conclusion: The decoupled approach of maintaining a frozen backbone while only training lightweight tokens for relative pose querying effectively solves the long video reconstruction problem, achieving superior accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods.

title: TokenMatch: 3D Mesh Correspondence Transformer with Curvature-Guided Tokenisation
comment: 25 pages, 13 figures and 12 tables; project page: https://4dqv.mpi-inf.mpg.de/TokenMatch/
summary: While data-driven 3D shape correspondence estimation has recently seen substantial progress, robust matching under partial observations and strong non-isometric deformations remains challenging. Existing learning-based approaches often rely on hand-crafted descriptors or template-based representations, whereas recent generative models over functional maps suffer from high inference cost, limited interpretability, and poor generalisation to partial shapes. In response to these limitations, this paper introduces TokenMatch, a new transformer-based unified model for estimating 3D shape correspondences. Our feed-forward approach trained exclusively on BeCoS, a challenging non-isometric partial-to-partial shape-matching dataset, can generalise to matching full shapes without retraining or fine-tuning. TokenMatch uses self- and cross-attention mechanisms to efficiently learn patch-level and point-level relations as well as dense correspondences between shape pairs. Our core insight is that meshes can be adaptively tokenised into patches using shape curvature guidance, enabling effective learning of shape-specific geometric descriptors for correspondence estimation. We evaluate TokenMatch on standard benchmarks for partial and full shape matching, including CP2P, PSMAL, BeCoS, FAUST, SCAPE, and SHREC'19. Our method achieves consistently high performance, in most cases outperforming existing methods for partial and full shape matching in the mean geodesic error and intersection-over-union metrics, while also running faster at sub-second inference speeds.

AI.tldr: TokenMatch is a transformer-based model for 3D shape correspondence estimation that can handle both partial and full shape matching without retraining. It uses adaptive tokenization based on shape curvature and self-/cross-attention mechanisms to learn patch-level and point-level relations, achieving state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks with sub-second inference speeds.
AI.motivation: Existing learning-based approaches for 3D shape correspondence suffer from limitations including reliance on hand-crafted descriptors, template-based representations, high inference cost, limited interpretability, and poor generalization to partial shapes. Robust matching under partial observations and strong non-isometric deformations remains challenging.
AI.method: TokenMatch uses a transformer architecture with self- and cross-attention mechanisms. It adaptively tokenizes meshes into patches using shape curvature guidance, enabling effective learning of shape-specific geometric descriptors. The model is trained exclusively on BeCoS, a challenging non-isometric partial-to-partial shape-matching dataset.
AI.result: TokenMatch achieves consistently high performance on standard benchmarks (CP2P, PSMAL, BeCoS, FAUST, SCAPE, SHREC'19) for both partial and full shape matching, outperforming existing methods in mean geodesic error and intersection-over-union metrics while running at sub-second inference speeds.
AI.conclusion: The proposed TokenMatch demonstrates that training on partial-to-partial shape matching enables generalization to full shapes without retraining or fine-tuning. Its transformer-based approach with curvature-guided tokenization effectively addresses the challenges of non-isometric deformations and partial observations in 3D shape correspondence estimation.

title: Temporal Self-Distillation: Learning Visual State Tracking in Videos Without Supervision
summary: We introduce S$^3$T (Self-Supervised Self-Distillation over Time), which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first fully self-contained framework for continuous video state tracking. Our method treats temporal sampling density as privileged information, based on the hypothesis that a denser view of the same clip recovers the running state more accurately. This view serves as the teacher, while a sparse-view student with the same weights learns to match its next-token distribution. The model generates its own target, so training requires no labels, separate teacher, or reward signal, and adds no inference cost. On LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B, S$^3$T improves VSTAT accuracy by $+1.74$ as a single model, $+2.38$ with souping, and $+2.70$ with additional vision-encoder adaptation, while prior self-evolving methods leave state tracking largely unchanged. The capability learned from unlabeled synthetic clips transfers to real videos, improving performance by $+7.95$ on VSTAT-YouTube state-tracking questions and $+4.50$ on MVBench Action Count.

AI.tldr: S³T is the first fully self-contained framework for continuous video state tracking, using self-supervised self-distillation where a denser temporal view serves as teacher to train a sparse-view student model, requiring no labels or separate teacher.
AI.motivation: Enable continuous video state tracking without external labels, separate teachers, or reward signals by treating temporal sampling density as privileged information - the hypothesis being that denser views of the same clip recover running state more accurately than sparse views.
AI.method: Self-supervised self-distillation over time: a denser view of a clip serves as the teacher while a sparse-view student with the same weights learns to match its next-token distribution. The model generates its own targets, requiring no labels, separate teacher, or reward signal, and adds no inference cost.
AI.result: On LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B: +1.74 VSTAT accuracy as single model, +2.38 with souping, +2.70 with additional vision-encoder adaptation. Transfer to real videos: +7.95 on VSTAT-YouTube and +4.50 on MVBench Action Count. Prior self-evolving methods left state tracking largely unchanged.
AI.conclusion: S³T successfully enables continuous video state tracking through self-supervised learning, with significant improvements across benchmarks and successful transfer from synthetic to real videos, representing a novel self-contained approach that generates its own training targets.
